assertion: The stage sweep's convention, not a claim about the game: every quest state item is undetermined until a run sets it, except that the quest whose stage the sweep sets is running, and that a stage a run sets counts as not done before (the sweep explores first settings); a quest whose running state is undetermined runs after one of its stages is set, and whether that started it is left open.
origin: Interpreter convention for quest_run stages (spec/vm.md, Quests); nothing to measure in the game.
live_measurement: None planned: a convention of the sweep. Its results are refuted only through the rules it combines.

assertion: A placed record (REFR, ACHR) whose XESP names an enable parent is present (drawn and colliding) exactly when that parent is enabled, unless flag bit 0 inverts it (xesp_flag_bit0_opposite_v1).
covered_causes: RuntimeEnableParent XESP (render and collision readiness, placed references and actors); DisabledThroughEnableParent in the draw build and collision
origin: Reading recognised from prior knowledge of the editor's enable parent field; layout from the published record definitions (spec/plugin.md). enable_parent_census: 39,461 placed records carry one 8-byte XESP (36,814 REFR, 2,497 ACHR, 93 PHZD, 57 PGRE), never two; every parent that resolves is a REFR, ACHR or PHZD in a persistent group (39,461 of 39,461).
live_measurement: In one launch, find a child whose chain says enabled and one whose chain says disabled (no opposite flag), photograph both places; then disable the enabled child's parent and enable the disabled child's parent by console and photograph again: a child seen while its parent is disabled, or missing while it is enabled, refutes it; walk into both for collision.

assertion: At the start of a game, a record without XESP is enabled exactly when its record header lacks flag 0x800; a record with XESP starts as its parent's start state gives through xesp_child_follows_parent_v1, followed up the chain to a record without XESP. A chain that ends in a cycle, at FormID 0, at an unresolved FormID or at a missing record, or in which a record other than the root carries its own flag 0x800, is not decided.
origin: Flag 0x800 as initially disabled is vm_host_is_disabled_flag_v1's reading; the chain rule recognised from prior knowledge. enable_parent_census: chains of depth 1 (38,101), 2 (1,331), 3 (29); 39,458 end at a record without XESP, 3 in a cycle; 19,763 children name a parent with flag 0x800; 866 children carry flag 0x800 themselves (not decided by this rule).
live_measurement: Same launch as xesp_child_follows_parent_v1, on a new game before any quest runs: for children of depth 1 and 2 whose roots carry and lack flag 0x800, photograph them where they stand; a child present against its chain's start state refutes it.

assertion: XESP flag bit 0 (byte 4) set inverts the link: the record is present exactly when its parent is disabled.
covered_causes: RuntimeEnableParent XESP.opposite (chains with bit 0 on any link)
origin: Bit meaning recognised from prior knowledge of the editor field ('opposite of parent'). enable_parent_census: flag bytes 0x00 (37,110), 0x01 (2,227), 0x02 (56), 0x03 (68), no other value; 3,012 chains use bit 0.
live_measurement: Photograph, in one launch, a child with bit 0 set whose root carries flag 0x800 (the rule says present) and one whose root lacks it (absent); toggle the root by console and photograph again: presence that does not invert refutes it.

assertion: XESP flag bit 1 does not change whether the record is present; it is preserved and only gates the chain under this rule.
covered_causes: RuntimeEnableParent XESP.bit1 (chains with bit 1 on any link)
origin: Bit recognised from prior knowledge as a fade ('pop in') choice, which would change how a record appears or disappears, not whether. enable_parent_census: 135 chains use bit 1 (50 alone, 85 with bit 0).
live_measurement: Photograph a child with bit 1 set and one without under parents in the same start state; then toggle the parents by console: the two children must be present and absent together once any fade has ended.

assertion: A script's Enable or Disable of a record reaches its enable children transitively: each child takes its parent's new state through xesp_child_follows_parent_v1 and xesp_flag_bit0_opposite_v1, as for the start state; a record's own Enable or Disable in the same run wins over its parent's state.
covered_causes: fo4-view --script-event (with vm_disable_hides_reference_v1); applies only to records whose chain is decided
origin: Interpreter assumption built on the rules above (spec/vm.md, Visible effect); recognised from prior knowledge of how the editor field is described.
live_measurement: Run the event in the game (activate the reference, as --script-event delivers it) and photograph the children of the toggled parent before and after: a child that does not follow its parent refutes it; then, by console, enable a child whose parent is disabled and check whether it appears (decides the precedence clause).

assertion: At rest no sequence of a NiControllerManager that does not loop plays: the manager, its sequences of cycle type other than 0, its object palette and its text keys leave the model's blocks as stored.
covered_causes: UnsupportedAnimationRuntime ...;rest=manager-idle (NiControllerManager, NiControllerSequence, NiDefaultAVObjectPalette, NiTextKeyExtraData, NiMultiTargetTransformController); render and collision readiness
origin: Candidate from the nifxml structure (a manager owns sequences that are started by name; TimeControllerFlags bit 5 Manager Controlled; CycleType) and controller_census (spec/controller-census.txt): 1,630 models with a manager; 545 models (22,607 placements) are decided by the rest rules, 395 of them with only clamped sequences and 150 with none. Looping sequences (manager-loop) and effect-shader controllers run by a manager (effect-idle) stay refused: a first version that counted them as idle drew the lobby and vault test views under a white veil of mist and light-beam effects. Models with a behaviour graph (BSBehaviorGraphExtraData) stay refused.
live_measurement: Photograph, in one launch and over several seconds without interacting, placed models with a manager, clamped sequences only and no behaviour graph: any part that moves, appears, disappears or changes texture coordinates against the drawing of the stored blocks refutes it.

assertion: A transform controller run only by a manager (Manager Controlled flag 0x20 in a model with a NiControllerManager), and every transform controlled block of a sequence that does not loop, with the interpolators and key data its links reach, leave their nodes at the stored transforms while no sequence plays.
covered_causes: UnsupportedAnimationRuntime ...;rest=idle-transform (NiTransformController, NiTransformInterpolator, NiTransformData, blend interpolators reached from a sequence or a manager-run controller); render and collision readiness
origin: Needs nif_controller_rest_manager_idle_v1; 21,967 decided placements rely on it. controller_census: sequence transform interpolators whose pose value is set equal the node's stored translation in 10,337 of 12,211 and its rotation in 6,874 of 7,244; their key at the sequence start time equals the stored translation in 3,701 of 6,062 (a stored pose is often an end pose, as for a door at rest).
live_measurement: Photograph a placed manager-driven model whose sequences move nodes (a door or a lift without a behaviour graph) at rest beside its drawing from the same camera words; walk into it for the collision: a node away from its stored transform refutes it.

assertion: An alpha, texture transform, lighting-shader float or colour, or light controller run only by a manager (flag 0x20 with a NiControllerManager, or a controlled block of a sequence that does not loop), with what its interpolator links reach, leaves its target's stored values while no sequence plays. Effect-shader controllers are not covered.
origin: Needs nif_controller_rest_manager_idle_v1. controller_census: 413 models carry such blocks, 164 decided placements rely on it; controlled variables by the nifxml enums (spec/controller-census.txt).
live_measurement: Photograph a manager-driven model whose sequences drive a shader's alpha or texture offset (a screen or a sign) at rest beside its drawing: a texture offset or a transparency other than the stored one refutes it.

assertion: A transform controller not run by a manager whose NiTransformInterpolator pose value (when set) and every key of its NiTransformData equal the target node's stored transform (translation within 0.001, rotation words within 0.001 through the quaternion read as rows, scale within 0.0001) leaves the node at its stored transform at every time.
origin: controller_census: the quaternion matrix read as rows equals the stored rotation words for 2,168 controller and 5,034 sequence interpolators, its transpose alone for none; 388 models carry such controllers, 605 decided placements rely on it. XYZ rotation keys are never read as constant.
live_measurement: Photograph such a model (no manager, every key equal to the stored node) over several seconds beside its drawing: any motion refutes it.

assertion: A controller not run by a manager that drives only a light (colour, dimmer, radius) or a lighting-shader term the reference frame does not draw (refraction strength, environment map scale, glossiness, specular strength, emissive multiple, specular or emissive colour; nifxml LightingShaderControlledFloat 0, 8 to 11 and LightingShaderControlledColor 0, 1) leaves the unlit frame unchanged.
origin: Frame scope: the CPU and GPU frames are unlit and draw no light, specular, refraction, environment or emissive term (spec/render.md). controller_census: 45 models, 91 decided placements rely on it.
live_measurement: Photograph such a model in the game over several seconds: a change of geometry, diffuse texture, texture coordinates or transparency (what the frame draws) refutes it; a change of brightness or glow does not bear on it.

assertion: A CTDA subrecord is 32 bytes: u8 at 0 holding the operator code in bits 5 to 7 and flag bits 0 to 4, three bytes unused, the comparison word at 4 (an f32, or a GLOB FormID when flag bit 0x04 is set), u16 function index at 8, two bytes unused, two parameter words at 12 and 16, the run-on word at 20, a reference FormID at 24 (set only for run-on word 2), an i32 at 28; CIS1 and CIS2 after a CTDA hold its text parameters.
origin: Recognised from prior general knowledge; no public page giving the layout could be read (the Creation Kit wiki redirected to a maintenance page on 2026-11-22). cond_census over every winning record (130,308 CTDA in 27 record types): every CTDA 32 bytes; flag bit 0x04 set in 10,005 and the word names a GLOB in all of them; clear in 120,303 and the word is a finite f32 in all (119,692 integral) and names a GLOB in none; operator codes 0 to 5 only; the reference word is zero for every run-on word but 2; bytes 1-3 and 10-11 not zero in 120,549 and 96,718 (kept as stored, no meaning read); CIS1 after 680 conditions and CIS2 after 12,162, never out of place; CIS2 after every condition of functions 629 and 660 and of no other, CIS1 after every condition of functions 447, 659, 660 and 675 and of no other.
live_measurement: Build, with an overlay plugin, a dialogue line or a stage log entry whose condition word bytes are changed one field at a time (function, a parameter, the comparison value, the operator) and check in the running game that the condition's result changes as the field predicts.

assertion: A condition list is the AND of its OR groups: a condition whose flag bit 0x01 is set is joined to the next condition by OR, any other by AND, and OR binds tighter than AND (A AND B OR C AND D is A AND (B OR C) AND D); the OR bit of the last condition joins nothing; an empty list holds. A condition that is undetermined leaves the list undetermined only when the determined conditions do not settle it (three-valued AND and OR).
origin: Recognised from prior general knowledge of how the editor documents condition lists; the documentation page could not be read (maintenance redirect, 2026-11-22). cond_census: 65,783 lists; 34,417 of one condition, 28,181 AND only, 1,604 OR only, 1,581 mixing AND and OR, where the reading matters; 3,093 lists end with the OR bit set. In the new-game state before any script runs 195 lists evaluate differently left to right (8 false here and true there, 182 false here and undetermined there, 5 undetermined here and true there).
live_measurement: In a purpose-built quest, give one stage two log entries with notifications, the first conditioned by GetStageDone(10) == 1 AND GetStageDone(20) == 1 OR GetStageDone(30) == 1 with flag bits as the rule reads them; set the stages so that the two readings (AND of OR groups, left to right) differ and set the stage: the notification shown settles the reading.

assertion: Operator codes 0 to 5 (bits 5 to 7 of byte 0) compare the function's value with the comparison value as numbers: 0 equal, 1 not equal, 2 greater, 3 greater or equal, 4 less, 5 less or equal; a truth value is 1 or 0. Codes 6 and 7 have no candidate meaning.
origin: Recognised from prior general knowledge; cond_census: codes 0 (104,953), 1 (10,186), 2 (2,221), 3 (4,421), 4 (6,794), 5 (1,733), never 6 or 7; the functions read here as truth values compare mostly with 0 or 1 under codes 0 and 1 (function 59: values 0 or 1 in 18,572 of 18,608, codes 0 or 1 in 18,597; function 56: values 0 or 1 in all 510, codes 0 or 1 in 509), function 58 uses all six.
live_measurement: One purpose-built stage log entry per operator code, each conditioned on GetStage of a quest whose stage is known, with a notification; set the stage once with the stage below, equal to and above the comparison value.

assertion: When flag bit 0x04 of a condition is set, its comparison value is the current value of the GLOB its comparison word names, not the word read as an f32.
origin: Recognised from prior general knowledge; cond_census: the word names a winning GLOB in all 10,005 conditions with the bit and in none of 120,303 without it. The evaluator reads the global as the data host does (vm_host_global_fltv_v1, vm_host_data_state_v1).
live_measurement: A purpose-built log entry conditioned on GetStage >= a global, with a notification; set the global with the console below and above the stage before setting it.

assertion: Flag bit 0x02 of a condition makes its parameters name aliases of the condition's quest and bit 0x08 package data, instead of FormIDs; bit 0x10 swaps subject and target. The evaluator therefore leaves a condition of an evaluated function with bit 0x02 or 0x08 undetermined, and evaluates one with 0x10 as without it, because no evaluated function reads the subject or target.
origin: Recognised from prior general knowledge; cond_census: bit 0x02 in 3,955 conditions, and in quests its first parameter names an alias of the quest in 3,308 of 3,320; bit 0x08 in 109, bit 0x10 in 30.
live_measurement: A purpose-built quest with an alias forced to a known reference and a log entry conditioned on GetIsID with bit 0x02 and the alias index as parameter: the entry's notification shows exactly when the alias holds a reference of that base.

assertion: Condition function 56 is 1 when the quest its first parameter names is running and 0 otherwise; it does not read the run-on target.
origin: Meaning recognised from prior general knowledge (no public index table was read; the index is kept bare in the census). cond_census: first parameter a winning QUST in 510 of 510, second parameter zero in all, run-on word 0 in all, comparison values 0 and 1 only.
live_measurement: A purpose-built log entry conditioned on function 56 of a second quest == 1, with a notification; set the stage with the second quest stopped, then started.

assertion: Condition function 58 is the current stage of the quest its first parameter names (the stage GetCurrentStageID answers); it does not read the run-on target.
origin: Meaning recognised from prior general knowledge (no public index table was read). cond_census: first parameter a winning QUST in 3,655 of 3,665 (10 zero), second parameter zero in all, run-on word 0 in 3,660; the comparison value is a stage index of that quest in 3,328 of the 3,655, all six operator codes used.
live_measurement: A purpose-built log entry conditioned on function 58 of a second quest >= 20, with a notification; set the stage with the second quest at stage 10, then 20.

assertion: Condition function 59 is 1 when the stage its second parameter names (an integer, not a FormID) of the quest its first parameter names is done, and 0 otherwise; it does not read the run-on target.
origin: Meaning recognised from prior general knowledge (no public index table was read). cond_census: first parameter a winning QUST in 18,592 of 18,608 (16 zero); the second parameter is a stage index of that quest in 17,902 of the 18,592; run-on word 0 in 18,596; comparison values 1 (11,208) and 0 (7,364), 36 other integers.
live_measurement: A purpose-built log entry conditioned on function 59 of a second quest's stage 10 == 1, with a notification; set the stage before and after setting stage 10 of the second quest.

assertion: Condition function 74 is the value of the GLOB its first parameter names; it does not read the run-on target.
origin: Meaning recognised from prior general knowledge (no public index table was read). cond_census: first parameter a winning GLOB in 10,818 of 10,818, second parameter zero and run-on word 0 in all. Values read as the data host reads globals (vm_host_global_fltv_v1, vm_host_data_state_v1).
live_measurement: A purpose-built log entry conditioned on function 74 of a global == 1, with a notification; set the stage with the global at 0, then at 1 (set from the console).

assertion: The conditions of a stage's log entries are evaluated when the stage is set, after it is marked done and current, in the state the run holds at that moment (stages done, current stages, running quests, globals as the data host answers them).
origin: Interpreter candidate recognised from prior general knowledge; nothing measured. quest_run stages: 538 log entry lists evaluated, 80 true, 35 false, 423 undetermined.
live_measurement: A purpose-built stage with two log entries, the first conditioned on function 58 of its own quest == that stage, each with a notification: the first entry's notification shows only if the stage is current when the conditions are evaluated.

assertion: When a stage is set (not when a setting is refused as already done), the quest's own VMAD scripts receive OnStageSet(stage, item) after the stage's fragment has run, inside the same SetCurrentStageID call (quest_stage_fragment_order_v1); item is the position of the log entry selected (undetermined when the selection is open, or when no entry holds). Alias scripts and the fragment script receive nothing.
origin: Event name and parameters read from the installed Quest script's declaration and from the handlers' signatures (all 193 handlers on quest VMAD scripts take two Int; no fragment script or alias script has one); the order relative to the fragment and the item's meaning are recognised from prior general knowledge, nothing measured.
live_measurement: A purpose-built quest whose stage fragment and OnStageSet handler each show a notification with the stage and item: the order of the two notifications settles the order, the item shown settles its meaning; an alias script with a handler shows whether aliases receive it.

assertion: SMEN, SMBN and SMQN records are, in this order: EDID (optional), PNAM (the parent node: an SMEN or SMBN; a word below 0x800 naming no record for an SMEN), SNAM (the previous sibling or zero), CITC (u32, the number of conditions that follow), conditions (CTDA with CIS1 and CIS2), DNAM (u32), XNAM (u32); then ENAM (a four-byte event code) for an SMEN, or MNAM and HNAM (optional u32), QNAM (u32, the number of NNAM), and NNAM (a QUST) each optionally followed by RNAM (u32) for an SMQN. DNAM, XNAM, MNAM, HNAM and RNAM are kept as stored words without a meaning.
origin: Tag roles recognised from prior general knowledge; no public page could be read (UESP answered HTTP 403 on 2026-11-22). story_census over 473 winning nodes (18 SMEN, 120 SMBN, 335 SMQN): every node read to the last byte in this order; CITC equals the conditions in all 473; QNAM equals the NNAM in all 335; every NNAM names a winning QUST (1,308); PNAM names an SMEN or SMBN in every SMBN and SMQN; a quest's ENAM equals the event code of every node listing it in 987 of 987 quests with both.
live_measurement: Change in an overlay plugin one quest node's NNAM to another quest and its PNAM to another branch, then raise the node's event in the running game: the other quest must start, and only when the new branch's conditions hold.

assertion: An event is offered to the tree under the event node of its code: a node whose conditions are false is skipped with everything below it; an event or branch node whose conditions hold offers the event to its children in the order the previous-sibling links (SNAM) give, and the first child that starts a quest ends the walk; a quest node acts as sm_quest_node_start_v1 says. A node's stored words (DNAM, XNAM, MNAM, HNAM, RNAM) do not change the walk. Where conditions are undetermined, or the children's links do not make one chain and more than one child would act, whether a quest starts is undetermined.
origin: Candidate recognised from prior general knowledge of the story manager; the tree's links are measured (story_census: depth 0 to 6 below the event node; 131 of 136 parents' children make one chain of previous links, 5 do not). The stored flag words vary (SMQN DNAM halves 0x0000-0x0003 and 0x0000-0x0006) and are not read, which this rule states and a measurement could refute.
live_measurement: In a purpose-built tree under the script event, two quest nodes in previous-link order whose conditions both hold, each listing a quest with an OnStoryScript notification: raise the event from the console or a script and see which quest starts; repeat with the first node's DNAM changed.

assertion: A quest node whose conditions hold offers the event to its quests in stored order: the first that is not running and whose own conditions after NEXT hold is started as Quest.Start starts a quest (quest_start_v1), then receives OnStoryScript with the event's keyword, location, two references and two values; a running quest or one whose conditions are false is passed over; when none starts, the walk goes on. Alias filling from the event is not modelled (the start is taken to succeed).
origin: Candidate recognised from prior general knowledge; the event name OnStoryScript and its six parameters are read from the installed Quest script's declaration. story_census: 1,013 distinct quests listed by nodes, 181 nodes list one quest, 152 list two or more.
live_measurement: A purpose-built quest node listing two quests, the first already running, each with an OnStoryScript handler showing a notification with aiValue1: raise the script event with a value and see which quest starts and what it shows.

assertion: Keyword.SendStoryEvent(akLoc, akRef1, akRef2, aiValue1, aiValue2) and SendStoryEventAndWait raise the story event of code SCPT with the receiver as its keyword, offered at once inside the call (sm_tree_walk_v1); SendStoryEventAndWait answers true when a quest started, false when none did, and is undetermined when the walk is. It is the only story event a run raises: the other event codes name things the world does (dialogue, location changes, kills and the rest).
origin: Native and parameter names read from the installed Keyword script's declaration; the code SCPT, and that it is the script event, recognised from prior general knowledge. story_census: the SCPT tree lists 476 quests, every one with ENAM SCPT; 90 call sites of the two natives, 46 with a keyword that resolves to a constant record (42 keywords), 35 of which a SCPT node tests.
live_measurement: A purpose-built script calls SendStoryEventAndWait on a keyword a purpose-built quest node tests and shows the result through a notification call; the node's quest shows a notification in OnStoryScript; repeat with another keyword.

assertion: Condition function 576 reads the story event being offered: its first parameter is a u16 selector and a two-character member code; with selector 0 the function is 1 when that member is the record its second parameter names and 0 otherwise. Only the members K1 (the keyword) and L1 (the location) of the script event are evaluated; every other selector or member, and the function outside a story event, is undetermined.
origin: Meaning recognised from prior general knowledge (no public index table was read). story_census on nodes: parameter 1 is selector 0 with K1 (153), L1 (37) or L2 (19), selector 2 with V1 (7) or V2 (1), selector 3 with F1 (9), L1 (15) or L2 (8); cond_census: hosts SMQN, SMBN and QUST (after NEXT), second parameter a KYWD (215), LCTN (60), zero (47) or FLST (1).
live_measurement: A purpose-built quest node conditioned on function 576 selector 0 K1 == 1 with one keyword: send the script event with that keyword and with another, and see whether the node's quest starts.

assertion: ScriptObject.RegisterForRemoteEvent(sender, name) called on a script instance registers that instance for the event of that name on the sender and returns true (for an object sender; otherwise nothing is registered and the answer is undetermined); UnregisterForRemoteEvent and UnregisterForAllRemoteEvents remove registrations (an undetermined argument removes all of the instance's). When the interpreter itself delivers an event to an object (OnStageSet, OnQuestInit, OnQuestShutdown of a quest; the events script_run delivers to a bound reference), every instance registered for it receives the function ::remote_<type>_<event> for a type the sender is, with the sender and the event's arguments, after the sender's own scripts and in registration order. Events the world raises (location changes, loading, combat, statistics) are never delivered.
origin: Native and parameter names read from the installed ScriptObject declaration; the handler names (::remote_<type>_<event>, first parameter typed by the declaring engine type) read from the compiled scripts: 683 such functions; delivery order recognised from prior general knowledge, not measured. quest_run new-game: 21 remote registrations, 2 for OnStageSet.
live_measurement: A purpose-built script registers in OnInit for a purpose-built quest's OnStageSet and shows a notification in its remote handler; the quest's own OnStageSet also shows one; set the stage from the console and read the order of the two notifications.

assertion: ScriptObject.RegisterForCustomEvent(sender, name) registers the calling instance for that custom event of the sender; SendCustomEvent(name, args) called on an object delivers to every instance registered for (that object, name), in registration order, the function ::remote_<name> with the sender and the arguments array; names compare without case. Unregistering removes registrations as for remote events.
origin: Native and parameter names read from the installed ScriptObject declaration; the stored event names (<script>_<event> in all 224 registering and 96 sending call sites) and the handlers (::remote_<script>_<event> taking a sender and a Var array) read from the compiled scripts; that the sender is the receiving object of SendCustomEvent recognised from prior general knowledge.
live_measurement: Two purpose-built scripts: one registers for the other's custom event and shows a notification with the first argument; the other sends it with an argument from an activation.

assertion: A custom event runs after the delivery or job that sent it has ended (queued), at the end of the queue, in sending order; not inside the SendCustomEvent call (nested, the alternative counted by quest_run --custom-nested).
origin: Candidate recognised from prior general knowledge; nothing measured. The two readings are run and compared (spec/vm.md, Events).
live_measurement: A purpose-built script shows a notification, sends a custom event whose handler shows another, then shows a third: the order of the three notifications settles it.

assertion: ObjectReference.IsDisabled of a reference that carries an enable parent (XESP) answers the state its chain gives under the enable parent rules (xesp_child_follows_parent_v1, xesp_initial_state_chain_v1, xesp_flag_bit0_opposite_v1, xesp_flag_bit1_not_presence_v1), with this run's own Enable and Disable of the chain's records taken as their state (xesp_script_change_propagates_v1); a chain those rules do not decide is undetermined; a reference without XESP answers as vm_host_is_disabled_flag_v1 says.
origin: Built on the enable parent rules (spec/enable-parent.md: 39,461 placed records with XESP, 18,517 chains say enabled and 20,941 disabled at the start); nothing measured.
live_measurement: Show IsDisabled through a notification call of a child whose parent is initially disabled, before and after a script enables the parent.

assertion: An effect-shader float or colour controller (BSEffectShaderPropertyFloatController, BSEffectShaderPropertyColorController), whether run by a manager's sequences or not and whether those sequences loop or not, shows at the frame's instant the first key (lowest time) of every keyframe interpolator that drives it; where that key equals the target field's stored value (within 1e-4, every component) and any set pose value equals it too, the field is drawn as stored. A looping NiControllerSequence whose controlled blocks all name such controllers is covered with them. Where the stored value differs from a first key the field is not settled and the model stays refused.
covered_causes: UnsupportedAnimationRuntime ...;rest=effect-first-key (BSEffectShaderProperty*Controller, their NiFloatInterpolator, NiPoint3Interpolator, NiBlendFloatInterpolator, NiBlendPoint3Interpolator, NiFloatData, NiPosData, and a NiControllerSequence of such controllers alone)
origin: Candidate from effect_census (spec/effect-surfaces.md): of the effect-shader controllers with keys, the stored field equals the first key in most and lies elsewhere inside the key range in a minority (export snapshots); the two readings 'at rest = first key' and 'at rest = stored value' agree only where they are equal, and only there is the field settled. The pairing of controlled variable and field (EmissiveMultiple with Base Color Scale, Alpha Transparency with the alpha of Base Color) is by nifxml names only. That a sequence's clock starts at its first key when the cell loads is recognised from prior knowledge, not from a source.
live_measurement: Load a cell with a looping UV-scrolling and an alpha-pulsing effect whose stored values equal their first keys; capture frames at load and at several later times: the frame at load must match the first-key draw, and a later frame that matches it only by chance refutes nothing; an effect already advanced or faded at load refutes the rule.

assertion: An effect-shader surface of a model settled by nif_controller_rest_effect_first_key_v1 has colour = texel RGB x Base Color RGB x Base Color Scale x (vertex RGB where Shader Flags 2 Vertex_Colors is set) and alpha = texel alpha x Base Color alpha (opacity) x (vertex alpha where both Vertex_Colors and Vertex_Alpha are set); a material (BGEM) named by the shader supplies base colour, scale, alpha, texture, UV and blend state in place of the NIF's. An empty texture is a white texel. A base colour x scale above 1 is drawn under effect_colour_clamped_before_blend_v1, a negative one is refused.
covered_causes: effect surfaces drawn under nif_controller_rest_effect_first_key_v1 (draw rule)
origin: Candidate from field names (nifxml Base Color 'Base color', Base Color Scale 'Multiplier for Base Color (RGB part)', Fallout4ShaderPropertyFlags Vertex_Colors and Vertex_Alpha) and effect_color_only_v1, not a format-derived rendering fact. Surfaces with greyscale-to-palette colour or alpha, falloff, environment map, refraction, a colour above 1, or vertex alpha below 1 under one of the two vertex flags alone are refused with named errors instead (spec/effect-surfaces.md). Falloff, and vertex alpha below 1 under Vertex_Colors alone, are drawn since under their own rules (effect_falloff_view_angle_v1 and its companions, effect_vertex_alpha_under_vertex_colors_v1); the greyscale palette and a colour above 1 likewise (effect_palette_sampled_clamped_v1 and its companions, effect_colour_clamped_before_blend_v1).
live_measurement: Photograph one placed effect with a white texture region over a known background under two materials differing only in base colour, then only in scale (both at most 1), then only in alpha; and one mesh with painted vertex RGB and alpha under the four combinations of the two vertex flags; compare channel ratios.

assertion: An effect surface with blending enabled (NiAlphaProperty Alpha Blend bit, or the material's alpha blend) is combined with what is behind it as source x F(source factor) + destination x F(destination factor), per channel, clamped to 0 to 1, with F as named by nifxml AlphaFunction (the material's factors under bgsm_blend_factors_alpha_function_v1).
covered_causes: effect surfaces drawn under nif_controller_rest_effect_first_key_v1 with blending (draw rule)
origin: Candidate: nifxml names the factors but not the operation or the clamp; the reference rasterizer already combines other blended surfaces this way. The census found SRC_ALPHA/ONE and SRC_ALPHA/INV_SRC_ALPHA on almost every blended effect shape.
live_measurement: Photograph an additive (6,0) and a normal (6,7) effect over black, white and mid-grey backgrounds; the additive one must brighten without darkening and saturate at white, the normal one must interpolate.

assertion: Blended effect surfaces are drawn after every opaque surface, without writing depth, farthest first: the reference rasterizer by triangle centroid distance with the list order breaking ties, the GPU viewer by instance in its transparent phase; intersections are not split.
covered_causes: effect surfaces drawn under nif_controller_rest_effect_first_key_v1 with blending (draw rule)
origin: Candidate ordering of the reference frame (spec/render.md), not a claim about the game's sort; No Sorter (AlphaFlags bit 13) is zero on every effect shape the census saw.
live_measurement: Photograph two overlapping blended effects whose order by distance flips as the camera moves; a fixed order in the game refutes the distance sort.

assertion: Soft depth fade (Soft_Effect, Soft Falloff Depth, the material's soft flag and depth), lighting influence and effect lighting (Effect_Lighting, Lighting Influence, the material's effect lighting) are left out of this unlit reference frame: they do not change the drawn colour or alpha.
covered_causes: effect surfaces drawn under nif_controller_rest_effect_first_key_v1 that set one of these terms (draw rule)
origin: Policy of the unlit reference frame (as for lighting terms of lit surfaces), registered because the game evidently fades soft effects near geometry; the frame is expected to show such surfaces more opaque where they meet geometry.
live_measurement: Photograph a soft effect crossing a wall at close range: if its edge against the wall fades, the frame differs there by construction; the rule is refuted for any surface whose look away from intersections differs from the frame.

assertion: With falloff enabled (Shader Flags 1 Use_Falloff, or the material's falloff flag) and RGB falloff not set, the falloff's angle is the angle between the surface normal and the direction from the surface point to the eye, and the Falloff Start Angle and Stop Angle fields are cosines of that angle: the frame takes the shape's vertex normals through the node and placement rotations, interpolates them across each triangle like UV and evaluates the cosine at every sample.
covered_causes: Effect surfaces with falloff drawn under nif_controller_rest_effect_first_key_v1 (draw rule, fo4_render::Falloff), always together with effect_falloff_cosine_absolute_v1, effect_falloff_linear_in_cosine_v1 and effect_falloff_multiplies_alpha_v1; without them the surface is refused (UnverifiedEffectSurface); a shape without a normal on every vertex stays refused (falloff-normals)
origin: nifxml (pinned copy) states the two end points ('At this cosine of angle falloff will be equal to Falloff Start Opacity'); which angle is not stated. That it is the angle between the normal and the direction to the eye is recognised from prior knowledge, not from a source. effect_census (spec/effect-census.txt, Falloff): 1,778 shapes in scope draw falloff; all but 15 (no vertex data, no placement) have a normal on every vertex. Interpolating the normal per sample is the reference renderer's convention, not a claim about the game's arithmetic. Registered first without code; narrowed to the angle when the falloff was drawn.
live_measurement: Photograph a placed mist volume or light beam with falloff from several known directions over a uniform background: its alpha must fall toward its silhouette as the angle to the eye grows; a fade fixed to the camera's forward axis, to world up or to the light direction refutes it.

assertion: The falloff cosine is taken by its absolute value: a face seen from behind (its normal pointing away from the eye) takes the value the same face would have seen from the front.
covered_causes: Effect surfaces with falloff drawn under nif_controller_rest_effect_first_key_v1 (draw rule, fo4_render::Falloff::factor)
origin: No source. Recognised from prior knowledge that two-sided surfaces are shaded with the normal turned toward the eye. The reference renderer draws the back faces of single-sided surfaces too (spec/render.md), which the game culls. Census evidence partly against it: 509 of 1,778 falloff shapes (9,735 placements of their models) store a negative cosine (an angle above 90 degrees), which the absolute value never reaches, so that end point only sets the slope; the signed reading would make such angles reachable on back faces.
live_measurement: Photograph a double-sided falloff card (a mist plane or light beam) from both sides at the same angle in one launch: equal alpha supports it; a card that vanishes or fades differently from behind refutes it in favour of the signed cosine.

assertion: The falloff factor is Falloff Start Opacity at the Falloff Start Angle cosine and Falloff Stop Opacity at the Falloff Stop Angle cosine, linear in the cosine between them and constant beyond either end; with the two angles equal the two opacities must be equal and the factor is their value. Opacities outside 0 to 1, and equal angles with different opacities, are refused (falloff-fields).
covered_causes: Effect surfaces with falloff drawn under nif_controller_rest_effect_first_key_v1 (draw rule, fo4_render::Falloff::factor)
origin: nifxml gives the two end points and names the opacities 'Alpha falloff multiplier at start angle' and 'at end angle'; the shape between them (linear in the cosine, linear in the angle, a smooth step) and the clamp beyond them are not stated. effect_census: every falloff angle but 8 is the cosine of a whole degree; start cosine above stop on 1,674 shapes, below on 96, equal on 8 (both opacities 0, 32 placements of their models); one shape (no placement) stores an opacity below 0.
live_measurement: Photograph a falloff sphere or a round mist volume over black at a known distance and read the alpha along a diameter: it must follow the opacity linear in the cosine (for 10 to 80 degrees, 1 to 0); a profile closer to linear in the angle or to a smooth step refutes it.

assertion: The falloff factor multiplies the surface's alpha (texel alpha x base colour alpha x vertex alpha where read) before the alpha test and the blend, like any other alpha factor; it does not change the colour. With RGB_Falloff (Shader Flags 1 bit 8) or the material's falloff colour flag set the surface stays refused (rgb-falloff).
covered_causes: Effect surfaces with falloff drawn under nif_controller_rest_effect_first_key_v1 (draw rule, the reference rasterizer)
origin: nifxml names the opacities 'Alpha falloff multiplier'; that the factor multiplies the alpha already formed and enters the test and the blend is this reference's reading. RGB_Falloff has no description in nifxml. effect_census: 109 NIF shapes and 1 material set RGB falloff (155 placements of their models).
live_measurement: Photograph a normal (6,7) and an additive (6,0) falloff surface over a mid-grey background at a grazing angle: the normal one must fade toward the background and the additive one toward no contribution, with no change of hue; a darkening toward black or a colour shift refutes it.

assertion: An effect surface with Shader Flags 2 Vertex_Colors set and Shader Flags 1 Vertex_Alpha clear multiplies its alpha by the vertex alpha, as when both flags are set. Vertex_Alpha set with Vertex_Colors clear is not covered and stays refused where a vertex alpha is below 1 (vertex-alpha-flag-alone).
covered_causes: Effect surfaces drawn under nif_controller_rest_effect_first_key_v1 whose shape has Vertex_Colors alone and a vertex alpha below 1 (draw rule); with every vertex alpha 1 the two readings agree and no rule is needed
origin: No source: nifxml names the two flags only. effect_census (spec/effect-census.txt, Falloff), every effect shape in scope with Vertex_Colors alone and a vertex alpha below 1: 2,075 shapes; of the 1,725 with an open boundary, 1,026 (37,418 placements of their models) have the boundary's mean vertex alpha at least 0.25 below the interior's and half or more of the boundary vertices at alpha 0, the pattern of an alpha painted to fade a card's edges; 213 have no lower boundary. No shape with falloff has Vertex_Alpha alone. That the effect shader reads vertex alpha whenever vertex colours are on is recognised from prior knowledge, not from a source.
live_measurement: Photograph, in one launch, a placed mist card whose vertex alpha fades to 0 at its edges beside a loose copy of its NIF with Vertex_Alpha added (overlay plugin pointing a copy of the base at it): identical frames support it; hard card edges in the shipped model refute it.

assertion: An effect-shader float controller (BSEffectShaderPropertyFloatController) driving Falloff Start Angle or Falloff Stop Angle (EffectShaderControlledVariable 1, 2) holds its key and pose values in degrees, while the shader field holds the cosine of the angle; under nif_controller_rest_effect_first_key_v1 such a field is settled where the stored cosine equals the cosine of the first key of every interpolator that drives it, read as degrees (within 1e-4; likewise any set pose value), and is then drawn as stored.
covered_causes: UnsupportedAnimationRuntime ...;rest=falloff-degrees, always with rest=effect-first-key on the same blocks (the controller, its NiFloatInterpolator or NiBlendFloatInterpolator and NiFloatData, and a looping NiControllerSequence naming it)
origin: The pinned nifxml copy describes the enum options as 'Falloff Start Angle (degrees)' and 'Falloff Stop Angle (degrees)' and the shader fields as 'At this cosine of angle falloff will be equal to ...'; it does not say how a controller's value reaches the field. effect_census (spec/effect-census.txt): all 146 falloff stop angle controllers in scope (the distant clouds, keys between 10 and 110) store exactly the cosine of their first key read as degrees, none stores the first key itself; no start angle controller is in scope. That the clock starts at the first key is nif_controller_rest_effect_first_key_v1's claim.
live_measurement: Through a loose copy of a distant cloud model whose stop angle controller keys are all set to one value k, photograph the cloud at load against a second copy with the controller removed and the field stored as cos(k degrees): identical fades support it; a fade matching the key read as a cosine or as radians refutes it.

assertion: The palette of a greyscale-to-palette effect surface (the shader's or material's greyscale texture) is read bilinearly at one level, the base level the frame loads, with both coordinates clamped to 0 to 1 and texel indices clamped to its edges (no wrap, no mip selection).
covered_causes: Effect surfaces drawn under nif_controller_rest_effect_first_key_v1 with GreyscaleToPalette_Color or GreyscaleToPalette_Alpha (Shader Flags 1 bits 4, 5, or the material's flags) and a greyscale texture (draw rule, fo4_render::Texture::sample_clamped); an empty greyscale slot stays refused (palette-texture)
origin: nifxml names the greyscale texture 'used as palette' and states nothing of its sampling. effect_census (spec/effect-census.txt, Palette): 2,302 effect shapes in scope set a palette flag; their palettes are 2D (2,218 vary by more than 32 of 255 steps along both axes, 67 only along V), mostly 32 x 32 BGRA8 (1,397 shapes), up to 512 x 512; 9 shapes name none. Wrapping would read the opposite edge at a coordinate of 1 (white texels against the first column), which the palettes' dark first column and bright last column make visible. Clamping and the single level are the reference's reading, not a source.
live_measurement: Photograph a placed palette effect whose source texture holds pure white texels (a coordinate of 1) over black: the colour of the palette's last column supports it; the first column's (a wrap) refutes it.

assertion: The palette lookup's second (vertical, V) coordinate is the surface's alpha before the palette: the base colour's alpha (the material's alpha where a BGEM is named) times the vertex alpha where it is read, clamped to 0 to 1. The same V serves the colour and the alpha lookup.
covered_causes: Effect surfaces drawn with a palette (draw rule, fo4_render::Palette::coordinates)
origin: No source. effect_census: the palettes grow darker and more transparent toward U = 0 and toward V = 0 (luminance and alpha non-decreasing along both axes on the coarse grid for 640 of 1,196 colour-only shapes and 268 of 499 alpha-only shapes; the distant clouds' palette is white with an alpha that rises toward the bottom right along a diagonal), the shape of a table indexed by two intensities, so the second coordinate is an intensity of the surface; which one is recognised from prior knowledge (the effect's alpha, which effect controllers animate on 2,099 controllers in scope), not settled by the data.
live_measurement: In one launch, photograph a palette effect through a loose copy of its model whose base colour alpha is set to 0.25, 0.5 and 1 (overlay plugin pointing copies of the base at each): a hue that walks along the palette's V axis supports it; a hue fixed by the texture with only the opacity changing refutes it.

assertion: With GreyscaleToPalette_Color the palette's horizontal (U) coordinate is the green channel of the surface's sampled source texel (after the UV transform and filtering).
covered_causes: Effect surfaces drawn with GreyscaleToPalette_Color (draw rule, fo4_render::Palette::coordinates)
origin: No source: nifxml names the flag only. effect_census: the source textures of palette surfaces are nearly grey (RGB spread within 32 of 255 steps on 2,132 of 2,302 shapes, more than 32 on 164) and the green channel carries the image on the colour-only shapes (deviation of green above 32 steps on 773 of 1,196), so the choice of channel moves U by at most 32 steps on most of them; green is recognised from prior knowledge, not from a source.
live_measurement: Through a loose copy of a palette effect's source texture whose red, green and blue channels differ (red 0, green 1, blue 0.5) photograph the effect: the palette's last column supports it; its first or middle column refutes it in favour of red or blue or a mean.

assertion: With GreyscaleToPalette_Color the palette's RGB at the lookup replaces the texel's RGB; the colour is then the palette RGB times the base colour times its scale times the vertex RGB where read, as effect_surface_texture_base_colour_v1 takes the texel's.
covered_causes: Effect surfaces drawn with GreyscaleToPalette_Color (draw rule, the reference rasterizer)
origin: No source. That the palette 'colours' a greyscale source is what the flag's name says; that the base colour, its scale and the vertex colours still multiply it is recognised from prior knowledge. effect_census: base colour white on most palette surfaces, scale above 1 on 1,657 of 2,302 (10 or more on 345).
live_measurement: Photograph a colour-palette effect under two loose copies of its model whose base colours differ (white and pure red): a red-tinted palette colour in the second supports it; the same colour in both refutes it.

assertion: With GreyscaleToPalette_Alpha the palette's horizontal (U) coordinate of the alpha lookup is the alpha of the surface's sampled source texel.
covered_causes: Effect surfaces drawn with GreyscaleToPalette_Alpha (draw rule, fo4_render::Palette::coordinates)
origin: No source. effect_census: on the alpha-only shapes the texel alpha carries the image (deviation of alpha above 32 steps on 365 of 499 shapes) where green often does not (the distant clouds' source is RGB 0.8 throughout with alpha 0.1 to 0.7; a glow sprite's RGB is 1 throughout); indexing by green would give such surfaces one alpha everywhere. That the alpha channel is the index is recognised from prior knowledge and supported by that pattern, not by a source.
live_measurement: Through a loose copy of the cloud's source texture with its alpha channel set to a horizontal ramp and its RGB unchanged, photograph the cloud: a density that follows the ramp supports it; a uniform cloud refutes it.

assertion: With GreyscaleToPalette_Alpha the palette's alpha at the lookup replaces the surface's alpha before the falloff (the texel alpha times the base colour alpha times the vertex alpha where read): those enter only through the lookup's coordinates; the falloff factor then multiplies it, before the alpha test and the blend.
covered_causes: Effect surfaces drawn with GreyscaleToPalette_Alpha (draw rule, the reference rasterizer)
origin: No source. The palettes of alpha-only shapes run from alpha 0 at U = 0, V = 0 to 1 toward U = 1, V = 1 (effect_census), which makes them an alpha curve of both inputs; multiplying the result by the base and vertex alpha again would apply those twice. Recognised from prior knowledge.
live_measurement: Photograph a palette-alpha effect under loose copies of its model with base colour alpha 0.5 and 1: an outline that erodes (a threshold moves) supports it; the same outline at half the opacity refutes it in favour of a product.

assertion: A surface colour above 1 (an effect's base colour times a Base Color Scale above 1, times the texel or palette RGB and the vertex RGB) is clamped per channel to 0 to 1 before the alpha test and the blend: the frame holds colour within 0 to 1 (RGB8 output, an 8-bit unsigned normalised target in the viewer, which clamps a fragment's output before blending). Alpha is not clamped.
covered_causes: Effect surfaces drawn under nif_controller_rest_effect_first_key_v1 whose base colour times scale exceeds 1 in a channel (draw rule; the reference rasterizer clamps every sample, a no-op at or below 1); a negative or non-finite one stays refused (colour-negative)
origin: Frame policy of this unlit reference (spec/render.md: no tone curve, no lighting, PNG RGB8), not a claim that the game clamps there: nifxml calls Base Color Scale a 'Multiplier for Base Color (RGB part)' with range 0 to 360 and the game's frame is not 8-bit. effect_census: 2,615 effect shapes in scope have a colour above 1, mostly white base colours with scale 2 to 10 on additive (SRC_ALPHA, ONE) blending (1,607 shapes); the distant clouds 1.5 on white. Clamping first makes an additive layer add at most its alpha; a wider range carried into the blend would add more.
live_measurement: Photograph an additive effect with base colour scale 5 (a fire or spark card) over a mid-grey background in one launch beside a loose copy with scale 1: equal brightness over the background where the texel is bright supports a clamp before the blend; a brighter result for scale 5 refutes it (a wider range reaches the blend).

assertion: The VMAD of an INFO or PACK record continues after its script list with a block: u8 version, u8 flags, the fragment script laid out as a script entry, then one fragment (u8, script text, function text) per set flag bit, lowest first; bit 0x1 is the begin fragment, 0x2 the end fragment and, for PACK, 0x4 the change fragment. A SCEN block is the same (bits 0x1 and 0x2) followed by a u16 count of phase fragments (u8 flag, u32 phase index from 0, then a fragment), flag 1 a phase's begin fragment and 2 its end fragment. A PERK block is u8 version, the script entry, a u16 count and entry fragments (u16 index of the record's PRKE entry, u16, then a fragment).
origin: Layout measured on every block of one installation (UESP answered HTTP 403 on 2026-11-22; slot meanings recognised from prior general knowledge). fragment_census: 2,396 INFO, 166 PACK, 632 SCEN and 32 PERK blocks read to the last byte; version 3 in all; the function name ends in _Begin, _End or _Change as the flag bit says in all 2,555 INFO, 188 PACK and 396 SCEN fragments; phase flag 1 with _Begin in 350 and 2 with _End in 386, 0 in 2 (not placed); phase index + 1 equals the two digits in the name in 736 of 738; PERK index equals the name's digits in 36 of 36 and is below the PRKE count in 35 of 36.
live_measurement: In a purpose-built quest, give one dialogue line begin and end fragments and one scene a begin fragment and phase 1 begin and end fragments, each showing a notification; play them in the running game: the order and presence of the notifications must follow the flag bits as read; then swap two flag bits with an overlay plugin and see the fragments change places.

assertion: A fragment of an INFO, PACK, SCEN or PERK block runs on one instance of the block's fragment script attached to the record's handle, holding the block script's VMAD property values; the parameters an INFO (the speaker), PACK (the actor) or PERK (target and actor) fragment receives are not known outside the world and are undetermined in the sweeps; SCEN fragments take none.
origin: Recognised from prior general knowledge; nothing measured. fragment_census: the named function is found in the compiled script with parameters (ObjectReference) for 2,544 of 2,555 INFO fragments, (Actor) for 177 of 188 PACK, (ObjectReference, Actor) for 34 of 36 PERK, none for 1,122 of 1,134 SCEN (2 take a ReferenceAlias).
live_measurement: A purpose-built dialogue line's begin fragment stores a value in a script variable and its end fragment shows it and the speaker's name through a notification call; a second line of the same topic shows the variable again: shared instance or not.

assertion: A SCEN record is, in order: EDID (optional), VMAD (optional), FNAM (u32), phases (HNAM empty, NAM0 text, start conditions, NEXT, completion conditions, NEXT, WNAM u32, FNAM and SCQS optional, HNAM empty), actors (ALID, LNAM, DNAM), actions (ANAM of two bytes, the kind; NAM0, ALID alias, INAM index, FNAM optional, SNAM start phase, ENAM end phase, kind-specific fields and conditions; ANAM empty), PNAM (the owning quest), INAM, VNAM, then optional CNAM, ACTV, CRIS, conditions, KSIZ, KWDA, SCQS, NNAM, TNAM, XNAM; action kinds 0 to 6 store a topic (0, 3, 5, 6), a package (1), a timer (2) or another scene (4).
origin: Tag roles recognised from prior general knowledge; no public page could be read. fragment_census over 4,773 winning SCEN: all read to the last byte in this order; PNAM names a QUST in all and equals the label of the group of kind 10 holding the record in all; start phase <= end phase < number of phases for all 24,958 actions; DATA of kind 0 names a DIAL in 13,503 of 13,542, PNAM of kind 1 a PACK in 3,328 of 3,328, LCEP of kind 4 a SCEN in 1,069 of 1,069, the topics of kinds 3 and 5 a DIAL in all but 5 to 7 each.
live_measurement: Change in an overlay plugin one scene's action end phase and one phase's completion condition, and observe in the running game that the action now spans the new phases and the phase waits for the new condition.

assertion: Scene.Start and ForceStart start a scene that is not playing when its owning quest (PNAM) runs: it plays, its begin fragment runs, then its phases (scene_phase_progression_v1); a scene whose quest is not running does not start; Start of a playing scene does nothing. Stop makes it not playing and runs no fragment. IsPlaying answers the state. At the start of a new game no scene plays; in the isolated scenario whether a scene plays is undetermined until a run starts or stops it.
origin: Recognised from prior general knowledge (native names read from the installed Scene script); nothing measured. Off with quest_run --no-scenes, which reproduces the earlier censuses byte for byte.
live_measurement: A purpose-built quest with a scene whose begin fragment shows a notification: call Start from a script with the quest stopped, then running, and show IsPlaying before and after Stop through a notification call.

assertion: A playing scene offers its phases in stored order: start conditions false pass the phase over; true enter it and run its begin fragment; it completes at once only when no action of the scene has start <= phase <= end and its completion conditions are absent or true, then runs its end fragment and offers the next phase; after the last phase the scene's end fragment runs and it stops playing. An action running in the phase (spoken lines, packages, timers, player dialogue, scene starts, radio), false completion conditions, or conditions the evaluator leaves undetermined keep the scene in the phase: the run does not advance it.
origin: Recognised from prior general knowledge; nothing measured. quest_run scenes: 4,773 scenes started in the isolated scenario enter 4,601 phases, complete 50, pass over 6; 32 run to their end; the others wait, most on an action (dialogue 2,495, player dialogue 689, package 660, radio 400, timer 165).
live_measurement: A purpose-built scene of three phases, the first with no action and no condition, the second with a completion condition on a global, the third with one dialogue line; each phase begin and end fragment shows a notification: start it with the global false, then set the global, and record the notifications and when they appear.

assertion: A scene whose FNAM carries bit 0x1 starts (scene_start_v1) when its quest starts, after the quest's start jobs (OnQuestInit, startup stages, and the stage whose setting started it), in the store's order of the scenes the quest's group holds.
origin: Bit meaning recognised from prior general knowledge. story_census: of 632 scenes with the bit, 539 are started by no constant Scene.Start call and no start-scene action the scan sees (85%), against 2,367 of 4,141 without it (57%).
live_measurement: A purpose-built quest with two scenes whose begin fragments show notifications, one with the bit and one without: start the quest from the console and record which notification appears.

assertion: Scene.GetOwningQuest answers the scene's PNAM; TopicInfo.GetOwningQuest answers the quest whose group of kind 10 holds the INFO.
origin: Recognised from prior general knowledge. fragment_census: every one of 102,433 winning INFO and 4,773 SCEN is held by a group of kind 10 labelled with a QUST; for every SCEN the label equals PNAM.
live_measurement: A purpose-built dialogue line's fragment shows GetOwningQuest() through a notification call; repeat for a scene fragment.

assertion: A game-time timer of h hours is due after h * 3600 / s real seconds, s being the value of the GLOB whose editor ID the caller names (the role of that global is an assumption): its stored FLTV until a run sets it with GlobalVariable.SetValue, then the value set; with s = 0 the game clock stands still and no game-time timer is due. Used only when a caller fires timers (quest_run --timers; without --time-scale-global the earlier stop is kept).
origin: Recognised from prior general knowledge; nothing measured. One GLOB carries that editor ID; the opening's stage 0 fragment sets it to 0.
live_measurement: A purpose-built script starts a one-second real-time timer and a 0.1-hour game-time timer with the time scale at 20, then at 0, and shows each OnTimer and OnTimerGameTime with Utility.GetCurrentRealTime through a notification call.

assertion: The run-on word of a condition names what a function that reads a subject reads: 2, the placed reference the reference word names; 5, the reference the alias whose index is the last word holds, of the quest the list belongs to (the quest itself for a QUST list, the owning quest PNAM for a SCEN list); every other run-on word (0 the host's own subject, 1, 3, 4, 6, 7 and above) names a subject the interpreter does not know, so a function that reads it is undetermined. Flag bit 0x10 (subject and target swapped) leaves such a function undetermined.
origin: Recognised from prior general knowledge (no public page read). cond_census: the reference word is zero for every run-on word but 2 (7,953 conditions; it names a placed REFR, ACHR or PHZD in 227 and an object id below 0x800 in 7,725); for run-on 5 the last word is an alias index of the quest in 287 of 287 QUST conditions; cond_blockers: run-on 5 in 585 conditions of function 72, the alias of the owning quest; the base of the reference function 72 reads is the record type its first parameter names.
live_measurement: A purpose-built quest with an alias forced to a known reference and a stage log entry conditioned, with run-on 5 and the alias's index, on function 72 against that reference's base (notification), and a second entry with run-on 2 and the reference word: both notifications show; change the base in the condition and neither shows.

assertion: Condition function 72 is 1 when the base object (NAME) of the placed reference it runs on (cond_run_on_subject_v1) is the record its first parameter names, and 0 otherwise. An alias that holds no reference, or a subject the interpreter does not know, leaves it undetermined.
origin: Meaning recognised from prior general knowledge (no public index table was read). cond_census: 17,964 conditions; parameter 1 a base record (NPC_ 17,736, FURN 67, STAT 53, ACTI 30, MISC 23, ENCH 12, TACT 10 and 8 more types) in all but 4 (zero); parameter 2 zero in all; comparison values 1 (17,715), 0 (247); run-on 0 (16,180), 1 (1,016), 5 (585), 3 (87), 7 (81), 2 (9).

Not evaluated: in alias fill conditions, where every one of them is, it runs on the candidate a fill search offers, which the interpreter does not perform.

assertion: A lighting shader (BSLightingShaderProperty) whose Name cites a material file that no mounted archive or loose folder holds is drawn as a lighting shader that names no material: with the shader's own UV fields and alpha, the first texture of its texture set and the NIF alpha property.
covered_causes: MissingMaterialEmbeddedShader: a MissingMaterial read by the draw build only as the Name of lighting shaders whose texture set has a non-empty first texture (fo4_scene::missing); render only (collision keeps render_inputs_collision_unchanged_v1)
origin: Candidate for the case the coverage census looked for (spec/materials.md): no placement of this installation needs it, since none of the 48,090 omitted placements with a missing material has a missing file read only as a lighting shader's Name (the missing files are swap sources and targets, material parents and 29 effect-shader names). The texture set is already read when the named material does not resolve (bgsm_name_overrides_texture_set_v1 suppresses it only for a resolved material). That the game draws the NIF's own texture set when the material is absent is recognised from prior knowledge, not from a source.
live_measurement: Photograph, in one launch, a placement whose model names an absent material beside the same model through a loose copy of its NIF whose shader Name is emptied (overlay plugin pointing a copy of the base at it): any difference in texture, transparency or visibility refutes it; an invisible shape or a default texture in the game refutes it.

assertion: A BGSM material whose Root Material Path names a file that no mounted archive or loose folder holds is drawn from its own fields, as every material is: the parent's fields are not read.
covered_causes: MissingMaterialParent: a MissingMaterial read only as a material's parent (fo4_scene::missing); render only
origin: Coverage census (spec/materials.md): 1,765 placements whose only missing file is read as a BGSM's Root Material Path (1,421 omitted for it alone, 0.55 % of the omitted area); every such file is absent from every mounted archive and loose folder, its file name nowhere. The draw build reads no parent field of a material whether the parent is present or absent, so the frame does not depend on the parent file; whether the game does is not known.
live_measurement: Photograph, in one launch, a placement whose material names an absent parent beside the same model through a loose copy of that material with its parent path emptied: any difference refutes it.

assertion: Where two or more material swaps apply to one placed model (a reference's XMSP with its base's model swap, or a SCOL's swap with its part base's), the material drawn for each shape is the one given by every one of four readings: the outermost swap alone, the innermost alone, each swap in turn from the outermost in, and from the innermost out. Where the readings differ for any shape of a base the base stays refused.
covered_causes: UnsupportedRenderSwapScopes whose readings agree (draw build); readings that differ stay refused unless mswp_outer_scope_wins_v1 and mswp_outer_scope_replaces_v1 settle them
origin: Coverage census (spec/materials.md): 3,316 placements refused for two or more swap scopes (a reference swap with a base swap 3,135, a SCOL part base among the scopes 181); the four readings agree for every shape of 1,032 (0.81 % of the omitted area), most of them where both scopes name one MSWP record, and differ for 2,284. No source states the order in which the game applies a reference swap and a base swap.
live_measurement: By an overlay plugin, place one model whose base swap maps material A to B under two references: one with a reference swap naming the same record, one with a reference swap mapping only another material; photograph both: a material other than the agreed one refutes it (and the second tells which reading holds where they differ).

assertion: A lighting-shader float controller (BSLightingShaderPropertyFloatController) driving a UV field (LightingShaderControlledFloat 20 U Offset, 21 U Scale, 22 V Offset, 23 V Scale), not run by a manager or run by a looping sequence, shows at the frame's instant the first key (lowest time) of every keyframe interpolator that drives it; where that key equals the field's stored value (within 1e-4) and any set pose value equals it too, the field is drawn as stored. A material named by the shader must hold the same value in that field (else UnsettledTextureMaterialField); elsewhere the model stays refused.
covered_causes: UnsupportedAnimationRuntime ...;rest=texture-first-key (the controller, its NiFloatInterpolator or NiBlendFloatInterpolator and NiFloatData, and a looping NiControllerSequence of such controllers)
origin: Coverage census (spec/materials.md): 4,716 placements omitted for texture-transform controllers alone carry lighting-shader UV controllers, none run by a manager or named by a sequence, each with stored U and V offset 0 and scale 1 equal to its first key; the shaders' materials hold the same UV values or the shader names none. That a controller's clock starts at its first key when a cell loads is recognised from prior knowledge, as for nif_controller_rest_effect_first_key_v1.
live_measurement: Load a cell with a scrolling-texture surface (a conveyor or a moving panel) whose stored UV field equals its first key; capture frames at load and several seconds later: the frame at load must match the first-key draw; a texture already advanced at load refutes it.

assertion: A textured surface samples its texture at, per component, stored UV x UV scale + UV offset, with the material's UV fields where the shader names one and the shader's otherwise; neither field is applied the other way round, and nothing else changes the coordinate.
covered_causes: UnsupportedUvTransform (draw build): a textured surface whose UV offset is not 0 or whose UV scale is not 1
origin: nifxml (pinned copy) names UV Offset ('Offset UVs') and UV Scale ('Offset UV Scale to repeat tiling textures') but states no order; the reference renderer has applied uv x scale + offset since its first version as its own convention (spec/render.md). Coverage census before this rule: 1,838 placements drawn without hypotheses (1.72 % of all area) and 15,009 drawn under hypotheses have a draw with UV offset not 0 or scale not 1; they now rely on this rule.
live_measurement: Photograph, in one launch, a surface through loose copies of its material with UV scale 2 and offset 0, with scale 1 and offset 0.25, and with scale 2 and offset 0.25: the texel at a known vertex under the third copy must be that of (uv x 2 + 0.25); (uv + 0.25) x 2 refutes it.

assertion: With the scene clock on, an action starts when its start phase is entered and holds every phase from its start to its end phase until it completes; an action whose time is settled (by a rule or a caller assumption) completes that many real seconds after it starts, on the real-time clock timers count on; the caller advances that clock to the next completion (quest_run --scene-clock N), and a phase whose spanning actions are all complete goes on to its completion conditions. An action whose time is not settled holds its phases as before.
origin: Prior general knowledge that scene actions run over a span of phases and that a phase waits for them; the real-time clock is the project's own reading. Nothing in the records was measured against it: the scene sweep and the forced opening only show what follows from it (spec/vm.md, Scene clock).
live_measurement: Run a purpose-built scene with a 2-second timer action spanning phases 0 to 1 and a phase-1 fragment that shows a message; time the message from the scene's start: 2 s supports it, a message at once after phase 0 rejects the spanning reading.

assertion: A timer action (kind 2) lasts the f32 its SNAM after the end phase holds, in real seconds; an action that also stores a TNAM (lower than SNAM in all 174) or has any FNAM bit set (0x80000 in 5) has an undetermined time.
origin: SNAM read as f32 gives round values (1, 2, 3, 5, 10 ... 86,000) in 1,198 of the 1,201 timer actions, 3 zero (spec/voice-census.txt, part 4); that it is seconds, and that TNAM may bound a random time, is prior knowledge not checked.
live_measurement: Time from scene start to the next phase for a timer action of SNAM 5 without TNAM (5 s supports it), and for one with TNAM 1 and SNAM 5 over ten runs (constant 5 s, constant 1 s or values in between decide what TNAM does).

assertion: A dialogue action (kind 0) completes once its line has played: the sum, over the line's responses in stored order, of the seconds the speaker's voice file declares; no pause between responses and no delay from the action's DMIN and DMAX are added.
origin: Prior general knowledge that a scene line waits for its audio; the pieces are separate rules (choice, path, speaker, seconds). DMIN 1 and DMAX 10 in nearly every dialogue action are not read.
live_measurement: Record the game's audio and the scene's next phase for a scene with one two-response line: the next phase starting within a frame of the audio's end supports it; a fixed gap or a gap equal to DMIN rejects it.

assertion: The line (INFO) a topic plays in a scene is the first in the stored order of its topic group (kind 7) whose conditions hold; an undetermined line before it leaves the choice undetermined; no line holding leaves the action's time undetermined; flags (ENAM) such as random or once are not read.
origin: Prior general knowledge of dialogue selection; 10,218 of 13,503 dialogue actions name a topic with exactly one line and 1,176 a topic with none (TIFC 0 in 1,153 of them; spec/voice-census.txt).
live_measurement: A topic with two lines whose conditions both hold, spoken ten times in a scene: always the first supports it; the second or a mix rejects it (random flag).

assertion: The voice file of response N of a line is sound/voice/<the line's plugin>/<the speaker's voice type editor id, lower case>/<the line's object id in 8 hex digits>_<N>.fuz, N the byte at offset 4 of the response's TRDA (20 bytes).
origin: Measured (spec/voice-census.txt): 155,282 of the 158,051 mounted .fuz entries under sound/voice have the shape; 150,249 of them are named by a response of their line; 85,445 of the 86,913 lines with responses have a file for every response, 1,468 none; 629 of 641 folders are VTYP editor ids; with the speaker's voice type settled from the records, its folder holds the topic's files in 8,243 of 8,265 dialogue actions.
live_measurement: Replace one response's file in an overlay archive with a tone of known length under the speaker's folder and play the scene: hearing the tone supports it.

assertion: The voice type of the actor speaking for an alias is the alias's own VTCK, else the VTCK of the base of its forced reference (ALFR), else of its unique actor (ALUA); an alias filled otherwise leaves it undetermined; a template's voice is not followed.
origin: Order is prior knowledge; measured support: the folder of the voice type so settled holds the topic's files in 671 of 682 actions (alias VTCK), 14 of 14 (forced reference), 7,558 of 7,569 (unique actor).
live_measurement: Override an alias's VTCK in a test plugin and play its scene: the line heard from the overriding voice type's folder supports the precedence.

assertion: A line (INFO) without responses that names another INFO in DNAM plays that INFO's responses, whose voice files are named with that INFO's id.
origin: Prior general knowledge of shared lines; measured: 9,206 of the 15,520 lines without responses have a DNAM naming an INFO, and in 9,133 of them that INFO has a file for every response (spec/voice-census.txt).
live_measurement: Play a scene whose line shares another's responses with a replaced file for the shared one: hearing it supports the rule.

assertion: A WMA-family file (tag 0x161) lasts its last dpds word divided by 2 x channels x sample rate seconds (the word read as decoded 16-bit bytes up to the end of the last packet).
origin: Prior general knowledge of the dpds table; supported without decoding by two header fields that were written apart: over the 154,738 mono voice files the stored data bytes grow with those seconds at 4,101 bytes per second against the declared average of 4,000 (2.5%), over the 544 stereo ones at 7,982 against 8,000, with a near-constant intercept of about 2.4 packets; within 5% of the fit in 87,775 and 289 files (spec/voice-census.txt, part 5). No audio was decoded.
live_measurement: Record the game's output while a known voice line plays alone and measure its length against the seconds the rule gives (within one packet supports it).

assertion: In player dialogue (kind 3) the player's topics PTOP, NTOP, NETO and QTOP pair with the answer topics NPOT, NNGT, NNUT and NQUT in that order; under a chosen choice the action lasts the player's line then the answer line, each timed as a dialogue line (the player's voice type is not in the records). Used only under the caller assumption --assume-player-choice.
origin: Letters read as positive, negative, neutral and question from prior knowledge; the stored order PTOP NTOP NETO QTOP NPOT NNGT NNUT NQUT in 2,929 of 3,159 actions agrees with the pairing (spec/voice-census.txt, part 4).
live_measurement: Pick each of the four choices in a purpose-built player dialogue action and note which answer line plays.

assertion: An engine event of a placed reference (activation, trigger enter or leave, opening) also runs on the script instances of every quest alias holding the reference, after the reference's own scripts (base VMAD then reference VMAD) and before the instances registered for it as a remote event; an alias holds the reference when a run's ForceRefTo set it, else, while its quest runs, when it is the alias's forced reference (ALFR) or, with the location reading on, its location special reference; quests in record key order, aliases by id, each handler with the arguments its declared parameters ask for (none, or the player for one object parameter).
origin: Prior general knowledge that alias scripts receive the events of the reference they hold; the order is the project's reading. Measured only that 2,204 setters sit in alias scripts and 1,912 more reach a set-stage call from them through a function passing a parameter on (spec/stage-setter-census.txt) and that the alias scripts' handlers declare the same signatures as the reference scripts'. Used only under the caller assumptions --assume-activate, --assume-trigger-enter, --assume-trigger-leave and --assume-open.
live_measurement: In an overlay plugin, give a placed activator a reference script and fill a quest alias with it, both with an OnActivate that shows a notification; activate it in the running game and note which notifications appear and in which order.

assertion: A placed reference (a door or a container) opening runs OnOpen(the opener) on its scripts and on the scripts of the aliases holding it, as vm_event_alias_scripts_v1 orders them; under the caller's assumption --assume-open the opener is the player.
origin: Prior general knowledge of the event name and its one object parameter; the compiled scripts declare OnOpen with one ObjectReference parameter on the engine's reference type. Used only under the caller assumption --assume-open.
live_measurement: Open a door with a script whose OnOpen shows whether its argument is the player, once by activating it and once through a script's SetOpen, in the running game.

assertion: For the stage-setter table, an engine event runs the script function of its name on the instance of the attached script (an engine event: a function without instructions whose name starts with on, declared by a script that declares a native function), a remote event the function ::remote_<type>_<event>, a custom event any other ::remote_ function, a fragment its slot's function; a call on self or a parent call carries an entry to the function it calls, within the attached script's chain. A function no entry reaches is counted apart.
origin: Reading from prior general knowledge of event names; 159 engine events found in 10,282 compiled scripts; 3,074 of 26,361 setters are in functions no entry of their own script reaches (spec/stage-setter-census.txt).
live_measurement: Not a game behaviour by itself: settled with vm_event_handlers_v1, vm_remote_events_v1 and the fragment rules; refuted by a set-stage call the running game makes from an event the table does not list for it.
