assertion: For the stage-setter table, a set-stage call (Quest.setStage or Quest.SetCurrentStageID on a quest receiver) sets the quest and stage its arguments give, resolved within the function: literals; self, GetOwningQuest() on self or on a property; a property by the values the VMAD of each attaching record stores (an int property without a stored value by its compiled initial value); a struct property's members together; any element of an array property; and a parameter by the arguments of each call of the function, followed outward up to three calls (Quest.SetQuestStage's struct parameter among them). Anything else is not a constant.
origin: The project's static reading of the compiled scripts. Measured: 8,494 set-stage call sites, 73 and 147 calls of functions passing a parameter on at depths 1 and 2, none at 3; 24,506 of 26,361 setters with a constant quest, 24,646 with a constant stage; 2,491 constant setters name a stage the quest record does not hold, mostly scripts whose int property has no stored value (spec/stage-setter-census.txt).
live_measurement: Not a game behaviour by itself; refuted by a stage the running game sets from a call the table resolves to another quest or stage (compare the table with the stages a save file records as done after the event).

assertion: The INFO field TIQS and the SCEN fields SCQS (scene level and phase level) are two little-endian i16: the stage of the owning quest set when the line, scene or phase begins (first) and when it ends (second), a negative value for none; the owning quest is the quest whose group of kind 10 holds the INFO, and the scene's PNAM. In runs (quest_run --stage-fields) a scene's and its phases' fields set the stage when the scene starts or ends and when a phase is entered or completed, before the point's fragment runs; an INFO's field is not applied (no run speaks a line).
origin: Tag roles from prior general knowledge. Measured over every winning record: 5,790 INFO carry TIQS, all 4 bytes; of the 5,875 non-negative halves 117 name no stage of the owning quest; scene SCQS 582 values (6 not a stage), phase SCQS 910 values (7 not a stage), one 2-byte SCQS in an action not read (spec/stage-setter-census.txt).
live_measurement: Watch a quest's stages in the running game (the console's stage query) while a scene with a phase SCQS plays, and while a line with a TIQS is spoken; the stage should be set when the phase begins or ends and when the line begins or ends.

assertion: A scene stopped in a phase on its start or completion conditions is offered that phase again whenever the run's quest state changes (a stage set, a quest started or stopped), and moves on as soon as the conditions hold. Applied only with quest_run --scene-recheck, after each caller action, timer firing and scene clock advance that changed the quest log.
origin: Prior general knowledge that a playing scene keeps testing its phase conditions; the trigger (a quest state change) is the project's reading. In the forced opening the first scene's last phase waits on a stage done and completes once the stage is set.
live_measurement: In an overlay plugin, give a scene phase a completion condition on a stage done, start the scene, then set the stage from the console after a pause; the phase should complete right after, not at the next scene start.

assertion: With the scene clock on, condition function 550 is 1 when the action of the scene its first parameter names whose INAM its second parameter gives has completed on the clock in the run, and 0 for an action not started or not completed. Applied only with quest_run --cond-550-clock; without it cond_fn_550_scene_action_complete_v1 stands.
origin: Extends cond_fn_550_scene_action_complete_v1 (prior general knowledge of the function; the second parameter matches an action's INAM in 412 of 416 conditions) to the actions the scene clock completes. In the forced opening a scene's phase waits on a timer action of its own phase and completes once that action is done.
live_measurement: A scene with a 2 s timer action and a later phase completing on function 550 of that action: time the later phase in the running game.

assertion: A start-scene action (kind 4) starts, when it starts, the scene its LCEP names, as Scene.Start would. Applied only under the caller assumption --assume-start-scene-actions, which also completes the action as it starts.
origin: Prior general knowledge of the action kind; LCEP of kind 4 names a SCEN in 1,069 of 1,069 actions (scen_record_layout_v1). When the action completes in the game (at once, or when the started scene ends) is not settled: that part is the caller's assumption.
live_measurement: A scene whose phase 0 holds a start-scene action and whose phase 1 begin fragment shows a notification: time the notification against the started scene's end in the running game.

assertion: A reference alias filled from a location alias with a location ref type (ALFA, ALRT), whose location alias is forced (ALFL), holds, while its quest runs and no run set its fill, the placed reference the forced location's special reference list (LCSR: 16-byte rows of a location ref type, a placed reference, its world or cell, a grid word) names for that ref type, when exactly one row does; otherwise it stays without a reference. Applied only with quest_run --alias-location-refs.
origin: LCSR row layout from prior general knowledge; measured: 300 LCTN lists all divide into 16-byte rows, every one of their 5,856 rows starts with an LCRT and names a placed REFR, ACHR or PHZD second; of the 2,850 aliases of this kind 790 resolve to one row, 494 to several, 419 to none, 1,147 have a location alias without a forced location (spec/stage-setter-census.txt, part 5).
live_measurement: Start a quest with such an alias in the running game and read its reference (the console's alias query); it should be the reference the location's row names.

assertion: Opcode 31 (the length of an array) on a none array stores 0 and the run goes on. Applied only with quest_run --none-array-length; without it the length of none is undetermined and blocks the branch that reads it, as before.
origin: Prior general knowledge (the length of an array never assigned reads as 0). The compiled scripts give no array variable a compiled initial value other than none; 9,845 array properties of the records' script entries are stored by no record, 8,597 of them behind a variable no instruction stores into, so they stay none until a script sets them, while the binder carries all 2,440 array values the records store (spec/array-census.txt). In the versioned censuses the length of none blocks 933 run outcomes (spec/vm.md, None arrays); the forced opening stops on it.
live_measurement: A test script (a loose .pex attached by an overlay plugin to an activator in a purpose-built cell) whose array property the plugin does not store shows its .Length through a notification when activated: 0 supports it; no notification with an error in the script log, or another value, rejects it.

assertion: Opcode 32 (an element of an array) on a none array stores the default of the element type (0, 0.0, false, the empty text, none for object, struct and var elements) and the run goes on with the next instruction. Applied only with quest_run --none-array-read; without it the run fails (NoneOperand), as before.
origin: Prior general knowledge (an array error is logged and the function goes on); nothing in the data says what the value is. In the versioned censuses opcode 32 on none ends 146 run outcomes (spec/vm.md, None arrays).
live_measurement: The same test script reads element 0 of the unset array property into an Int and then shows a notification with it: a notification showing 0 supports it; no notification (the function stopped) or another value rejects it.

assertion: Opcodes 34 and 40 (find a value, find a struct by a member) on a none array store -1 and the run goes on. Applied only with quest_run --none-array-find; without it the run fails (NoneOperand), as before.
origin: Prior general knowledge (a find that cannot look reports not found). In the versioned censuses opcode 34 on none ends 451 run outcomes and opcode 40 on none 5 (spec/vm.md, None arrays).
live_measurement: The same test script shows the result of Find on the unset array property: -1 supports it; no notification or another value rejects it.

assertion: Opcodes 33 (set an element), 42 (add), 43 (insert), 45 (remove) and 46 (clear) on a none array change nothing, make no array, and the run goes on. Applied only with quest_run --none-array-change; without it the run fails (NoneOperand), as before.
origin: Prior general knowledge (an array error is logged and the function goes on); whether adding to none makes an array is not settled by anything read. In the versioned censuses opcode 42 on none ends 423 run outcomes and opcode 46 on none 111; 33, 43 and 45 meet none in none of them (spec/vm.md, None arrays).
live_measurement: The same test script adds a value to the unset array property and shows its .Length and a notification after it: the notification with 0 (under pex_array_none_length_v1) supports it; 1 (add made an array) or no notification rejects it.

assertion: When the scene clock times a dialogue action (kind 0), or a player dialogue action (kind 3) under an assumed choice, the line it plays sets the stages of its TIQS (record_set_stage_fields_v1) on the line's owning quest: the first half when the line begins (the action's start; for the answer of player dialogue, when the player's line ends), the second when it ends (the second its timing gives). The line is known only when exactly one line of the topic has conditions that hold and every other line's are false; several lines that hold, or one whose conditions are undetermined, leave it undetermined unless the caller assumes the first in stored order plays (--assume-first-line, counted as an assumption). Applied only with quest_run --line-stage-fields; without it no line sets a stage, as before.
origin: Prior general knowledge of the field's role (as record_set_stage_fields_v1) and that a scene line is one line of its topic chosen by its conditions (scene_dialogue_line_choice_v1 chooses the first; this rule asks for a single line, as the choice among several is not read). In the forced opening the switch decides the line of 51 timed actions (each the only line of its topic that holds; 16 more are undetermined on conditions) and sets four stages, three first halves and one second half (spec/quest-run-opening.txt, spec/vm.md, Line stage fields).
live_measurement: Watch the owning quest's stages in the running game (the console's stage query) while a scene speaks a line with a TIQS whose topic holds one line: the first stage set as the line begins and the second as it ends supports it; a stage set at another point, or not at all, rejects it.

assertion: The environment map term of an effect surface (Shader Flags 1 Environment_Mapping, or the material's environment mapping flag; a cube map read along some reflection direction, weighted by the environment mask where one is named and by the environment map scale) only adds light to the surface's colour: it does not change the surface's alpha, its coverage, its alpha test or blend, nor the other colour terms (texture or palette, base colour and scale, vertex colour, falloff).
covered_causes: Effect surfaces drawn under nif_controller_rest_effect_first_key_v1 whose drawn fields set environment mapping (draw rule, with effect_environment_left_out_v1); refraction, fire refraction and the other features stay refused by name
origin: No source: nifxml names the flag, the Environment Map Texture, Environment Mask Texture and Environment Map Scale fields and the material's environment slots, and states nothing of how they combine. effect_census (spec/effect-census.txt, Environment map): 394 effect shapes in scope set it (310 through the NIF flag, 84 through a BGEM); every environment slot names a cube map of 6 faces that the texture reader decodes (BGRA8 128 x 128 on 363 shapes, BC1 32 x 32 on 31); the mask slot is empty on 314; 317 also name a normal map. That an environment map is a reflection added to the colour is recognised from prior knowledge of the shader family, not from the data.
live_measurement: In one launch, photograph a placed environment-mapped effect (a lantern bottle or a muck pool) beside a placement of a loose copy of its model whose Environment Map Scale is 0 (and, for a BGEM, a loose material copy with the flag cleared): the same outline and opacity with only a brighter or tinted colour in the original supports it; an outline, an opacity or a base colour that changes refutes it.

assertion: This unlit reference frame leaves the environment map term of an effect surface out: the surface is drawn with every other term as its rules give them. Under effect_environment_adds_to_colour_v1 the drawn colour is then a lower bound of the colour with the term (every blend the frame draws grows with the source colour).
covered_causes: Effect surfaces drawn under nif_controller_rest_effect_first_key_v1 whose drawn fields set environment mapping (draw rule)
origin: Policy of the unlit reference frame, not a claim that the game leaves the term out: the frame draws lighting-shader surfaces from their diffuse texture alone (no environment map, normal map or specular) and leaves effect lighting out (effect_soft_lighting_left_out_v1). Drawing the term would need at least five conventions no source gives (the world-to-cube axes, the reflection's normal, the mask channel, the weight of the scale, the combination with the base colour); 317 of the 394 shapes name a normal map, which the frame never reads, so a reflection from vertex normals would contradict their own data. The cube maps are read and decode (effect_census), so the term can be added later under its own rules.
live_measurement: The measurement of effect_environment_adds_to_colour_v1 bounds this one: the difference between the original and the scale-0 copy is what the frame leaves out; a difference larger than the clamp of a bright layer would show (more than a few 8-bit steps over the surface) marks the frame as a lower bound there, and a darker original refutes the lower bound.

assertion: Where a shape's effect material (the BGEM its shader names, after any material swap of the base or the reference) holds a value of a field an effect-shader controller drives that differs from the NIF shader's stored value (which nif_controller_rest_effect_first_key_v1 settled as the controller's first key), the frame draws the material's value: the material replaces the field, and the controller does not override it at the frame's instant.
covered_causes: UnsettledEffectMaterialField (draw build) where both values exist; a driven field without a pairing to a material field stays refused
origin: No source. effect_census (spec/effect-census.txt, Controlled fields under material swaps): 88 swap pairs replace a material whose shapes have effect controllers; 31 driven-field comparisons differ from the NIF's stored value (which equals the first key in all of them): 12 alpha fields, all below the first key and all driven by controllers whose keys hold one value; 9 U and 9 V offsets (0.005 and 0.035 against 0, keys that scroll); 1 base colour scale. 7 of the 12 differing alpha fields come from swap pairs that change nothing but the alpha, 4 from pairs that change the alpha and the base colour scale; under the opposite reading (the controller's first key wins) the first 7 swaps would draw exactly as the unswapped model, which a swap made only to change that field makes unlikely. Without swaps the NIF and its own BGEM differ on 6 of 350 driven fields (5 base colour scales, 1 base colour). The opposite reading is the rest rule's own premise (a running controller writes its key); the data only weighs against it.
live_measurement: In one launch, photograph a placement whose base swaps an effect material to one with a lower alpha (a dim light beam or glow) beside a placement of the same model without the swap, at the moment the cell loads and a few seconds later: a dimmer swapped placement supports it; the same brightness refutes it (the controller's key wins).

assertion: On a surface with blending enabled whose opacity (the material's Alpha, or the NIF shader's alpha or base colour alpha) is above 1, the sampled alpha times the opacity is compared by the alpha test as it stands, then reaches the blend clamped to 0 to 1: SRC_ALPHA and INV_SRC_ALPHA weigh the source by at most 1 and the destination by at least 0.
covered_causes: UnsupportedRenderAlpha from an opacity above 1 with blending enabled (draw build, lighting and effect surfaces, BGSM, BGEM or NIF fields); the reference rasterizer and the viewer apply the clamp to every blended sample, a no-op at or below 1
origin: No source. blend_opacity_census (spec/render.md, Opacity above 1 with blending): 103 winning materials blend with an opacity above 1 (59 BGSM, all SRC_ALPHA / INV_SRC_ALPHA; 44 BGEM, 7 of them additive), opacities from just above 1 to above 3; their textures' alpha times the opacity exceeds 1 on part of the texels for most of them (on half or more for 3,517 of 4,407 lighting shapes that name them), so clamped and unclamped blends differ there. Unclamped, an opacity of 2 with SRC_ALPHA / INV_SRC_ALPHA gives twice the source minus the destination, a result outside the colours of either; in the coverage census before this rule, 28,510 omitted placements (28.7 % of the omitted area) were refused for it (262 of them through a NIF alpha property, the rest through a material). An 8-bit target clamps a fragment's output before blending (the viewer's); the game's targets are not known to be 8-bit, so the clamp is a reading of the opacity as a contrast on the texture's alpha mask, not a sourced fact.
live_measurement: In one launch, photograph a blended cliff or debris layer whose material stores Alpha 2 over a known background, beside a loose material copy with Alpha 1: a layer whose mask edge tightens while its interior stays the texture's colour supports it; colours brighter or darker than both the texture and the background (an unclamped extrapolation) refute it.

assertion: A placed activator reference whose XPRM kind word is 1 is a box: half extents the three bound words times the reference's scale (XSCL, 1 without it), centred on the reference's DATA position and turned by its DATA rotation (the ZYX convention of the placement transform). Applied only with quest_run --trigger-box (with --track); without it no box is read, as before.
origin: Prior general knowledge (a primitive's bounds read as half sizes) checked against the data: XPRM is 32 bytes on all 30,028 placed references that carry one, its kind word 1 on 27,204 (6,929 activators) and its bound words three positive values not all equal on 26,975 of them; of 4,106 upright unscaled boxes of activators with a trigger handler, 345 have their bottom within 1 unit of the highest navigation mesh plane at or below their centre under the half-extent reading against 10 under the full-extent reading (spec/world-census.txt, section 3). Whether the scale applies and whether the box is what the engine tests is not settled by anything read.
live_measurement: In a purpose-built cell, place a trigger activator with a box primitive of bounds 100 x 20 x 100 whose OnTriggerEnter shows a notification; walk slowly toward it along its long axis from far away with the console's position readout: the notification at 100 units from the centre (not 50) supports it; repeat with the reference scaled 2 (notification at 200 supports the scale).

assertion: A placed activator reference whose XPRM kind word is 2 is a sphere of radius the first bound word times the reference's scale, centred on its DATA position. Applied only with quest_run --trigger-sphere (with --track); without it no sphere is read, as before.
origin: Prior general knowledge of kind 2 as a sphere, checked against the data: of the 220 XPRM of kind 2 (202 on activators, 18 on statics) all have three equal bound words (spec/world-census.txt, section 1). Whether the bound is the radius or the diameter is not settled.
live_measurement: As for the box: a sphere trigger of bound 100 shows its notification at 100 units from the centre (radius) or at 50 (diameter).

assertion: A trigger holds the player while the player's reference point (the track's position) lies in its closed volume; the hold starts and ends where the track's straight moves cross the volume's faces, and a move that only touches the volume for an instant raises nothing. Applied only with quest_run --trigger-point (with --track); --trigger-body is the alternative reading; with neither no trigger event is raised.
origin: Prior general knowledge that the reference position of an actor is at its feet; nothing read says which part of the player a trigger tests. In the forced opening the point reading misses one of the eight triggers the caller assumed before: its box's bottom is 6 units above the navigation mesh under the walked track (spec/quest-run-opening.txt).
live_measurement: In a purpose-built cell, a trigger box whose bottom is 40 units above the floor (its OnTriggerEnter shows a notification): walking under it raises the notification (rejects the point reading, supports a body) or not (supports it).

assertion: A trigger holds the player while a vertical segment from the player's reference point up a caller-given height (quest_run --trigger-body HEIGHT, a caller assumption of the player's height) meets its closed volume; holds start and end where the track's moves bring the segment to the volume's faces, an instant's touch raising nothing. Applied only with --trigger-body; --trigger-point is the alternative reading.
origin: Prior general knowledge that the engine tests a body (a capsule) against trigger shapes, reduced here to a vertical segment; the height (120 in the forced opening) is the caller's. With it all eight triggers the caller assumed in the forced opening are entered by the walked track (spec/quest-run-opening.txt).
live_measurement: The same raised box as for world_trigger_point_v1 at several heights above the floor: the greatest height at which walking under it still raises the notification measures the body's reach; a notification for a box above any standing height rejects the segment.

assertion: Trigger enter and leave are raised at the second the trigger's hold of the player changes on the real-time clock (the track's moves taken as continuous), after the timers and the scene clock steps due at that same second and before a caller's action due then, with the quest jobs the handlers bring run before anything later. Applied only with quest_run --trigger-instant (with --track); without it no trigger event is raised.
origin: Not read from any data: a reading chosen to be exact on the track. In the running game the event comes from the physics simulation's steps, some frames after the overlap begins.
live_measurement: Time, against the game's frame counter, the notification of a trigger crossed at a known speed in a purpose-built cell: a delay of more than a few frames after the crossing (from the position readout) bounds the error of the reading; order a timer due on the same frame against the trigger's notification.

assertion: A disabled trigger reference (by its initially-disabled flag, its enable parent chain or the run's own Enable and Disable, as IsDisabled answers) or one the run deleted (Delete) holds no one (a deletion with the player inside raises nothing); enabling it with the player inside raises its enter, disabling it with the player inside raises its leave. Applied only with quest_run --trigger-enabled (with --track); without it the crossing of a disabled trigger raises nothing and nothing is raised when one is enabled or disabled with the player inside (counted).
origin: Prior general knowledge that a disabled reference has no collision. 178 of the box activators and 3 of the sphere activators with a primitive are initially disabled, 491 and 9 have an enable parent (spec/world-census.txt, section 2).
live_measurement: Stand inside a disabled trigger with an enter notification and enable it from the console: a notification supports the second half; walk through it while disabled: no notification supports the first.

assertion: Several trigger events due at one second are raised leaves first, then enters, each in reference key order (plugin, then object id). Applied only with quest_run --trigger-order (with --track); without it several events at one second are none of them raised (counted).
origin: Not read from any data: a deterministic order chosen for the run. In the forced opening two triggers share one box exactly and are always entered at one second.
live_measurement: Two overlapping trigger boxes of different FormIDs whose enter handlers append to one quest-level list; read the list after walking in: the order across several entries decides it (a fixed order by FormID supports it; another fixed order or a varying one rejects it).

assertion: RegisterForDistanceLessThanEvent and RegisterForDistanceGreaterThanEvent keep a registration of the calling instance for two objects (an alias standing for the reference it holds) and a threshold; the event (OnDistanceLessThan or OnDistanceGreaterThan) is raised on that instance, with the two references and the threshold, at the first second at or after the registration at which the distance between the two objects' reference points is at or below (less than) or at or above (greater than) the threshold, including at once when it already holds; UnregisterForDistanceEvents removes the instance's registrations of the two objects. One object must be the player on the track and the other a placed reference standing still, or both standing still; an actor's position is open. Applied only with quest_run --distance-events (with --track); without it the natives are recorded as before and nothing is raised.
origin: Prior general knowledge of the natives' purpose; their parameters and the handlers' parameters are read from the compiled scripts (two script objects and a float; two object references and a float). 42 less-than and 15 greater-than call sites, 19 unregistrations, 25 scripts with a less-than handler and 12 with a greater-than one (spec/world-census.txt, section 5).
live_measurement: A test script registers a less-than event between the player and a marker with threshold 300 and shows a notification in the handler; walk toward the marker reading the console's position: the notification at 300 units supports it; registering while already inside: a notification at once supports the at-once half.

assertion: A distance registration ends when its event is raised: it is raised at most once. Applied only with quest_run --distance-once (with --distance-events); without it a registration whose event was raised stays but is not raised again (counted), the repeated reading being undecided.
origin: Prior general knowledge. The opening quest's handler unregisters the two objects itself after each event, which neither reading contradicts.
live_measurement: With the same test script without an unregistration, walk away and back within the threshold: a second notification rejects it.

assertion: A placed reference that is not an actor stands at its DATA position (and faces its third DATA rotation word, in degrees) in its cell's space (the worldspace of an exterior cell, else the interior cell) until a native of the run that moves it (MoveTo, SetPosition, MoveToNode, MoveToNearestNavmeshLocation, MoveToMyEditorLocation, TranslateTo) is called on it; an actor's position is open (no actor movement model). Applied only with quest_run --placed-positions (with --track); without it every placed reference's position is open.
origin: Prior general knowledge that a placed static keeps its editor position; the positions are the records' own. The exterior grid of 4,096 units holds every one of the 1,026,944 temporary placed references of exterior cells in its own cell's square (spec/world-census.txt, section 4).
live_measurement: From the console, read GetPos of a few markers and statics the scripts never move against their DATA: equal values support it.

assertion: GetPositionX, GetPositionY and GetPositionZ answer the position of the receiver (the player from the track, a placed reference under world_placed_position_v1); GetDistance the distance between the two reference points in three dimensions when both are in one space (two spaces: undetermined); GetAngleZ the facing in degrees (the track's facing for the player, the third DATA rotation word converted for a placed reference). Applied only with quest_run --position-natives (with --track); without them these natives are answered as before.
origin: Prior general knowledge of the natives' meaning; their declarations (receiver ObjectReference, results Float) are the compiled scripts'. Call sites: GetDistance 201, GetPositionX 54, Y 41, Z 55, GetAngleZ 42 (spec/world-census.txt, section 5). The angle's unit and sign are not settled.
live_measurement: From the console, compare GetPos and GetAngle of the player and of a marker with what a script's GetPositionX, GetDistance and GetAngleZ show in notifications at the same moment.

assertion: GetParentCell answers the interior cell the receiver is in, or in a worldspace the exterior cell of that worldspace whose XCLC grid square of 4,096 units holds its position; GetWorldSpace the worldspace, none in an interior; Cell.IsInterior whether the store indexes the cell as interior. Applied only with quest_run --cell-natives (with --track); without them these natives are answered as before.
origin: Prior general knowledge of the natives; the grid size is the data's own (all 1,026,944 temporary placed references of exterior cells lie in their cell's square, spec/world-census.txt, section 4). Persistent references and the engine's handling of positions on a square's edge are not settled.
live_measurement: A notification of GetParentCell for the player standing on both sides of an exterior cell border (console position readout): the cell switching at the multiple of 4,096 supports it.

assertion: GetCurrentLocation answers the location (XLCN) of the parent cell given by world_cell_natives_v1; a cell without XLCN leaves it undetermined. Applied only with quest_run --location-native together with --cell-natives (with --track); without them it is answered as before.
origin: Prior general knowledge that a cell names its location. Exterior cells without XLCN, and locations set by encounter zones or by scripts, are not settled. 172 call sites (spec/world-census.txt, section 5).
live_measurement: A notification of GetCurrentLocation for the player in an interior and in exterior cells with and without XLCN.

assertion: Where two or more material swaps apply to one placed model (a reference's XMSP over its base's model swap; a SCOL's swap over a part base's) and the readings of mswp_scopes_readings_agree_v1 differ, each swap is compared with the material path the model's shader names, not with a material another swap put in its place; where the outermost swap (the reference's, or the SCOL's over its part's) maps that path, its target is drawn, whatever an inner swap maps the same path to.
covered_causes: UnsupportedRenderSwapScopes readings differ (draw build, fo4_render::draw::settle) where the outermost swap maps the material and no swap of the stack maps a material another puts in place; chained stacks stay refused (UnsupportedRenderSwapScopes readings differ, chained)
origin: No source states the order. Probe of the references of the 3,678 placements refused for differing readings in the census before these rules (one installation; names kept outside the repository): one material the model names is mapped by both scopes to different targets in 2,572 placements (about half of the family's area proxy), by the outer scope alone in 686, by the inner scope alone in 779; a swap maps a material another swap puts in place in only 46. The reference swaps are written against the model's own material names (general swaps also used on bases without swaps), not against the base swap's targets; under the opposite precedence (inner wins) the reference's entry for the shared material would never show, and under the inner-swap-alone reading the reference swap would never show at all. A design argument from the data, not a measurement.
live_measurement: By an overlay plugin, place one model whose base swap maps material A to B under a reference whose own swap maps A to C and nothing else; photograph it: C supports the rule, B refutes it (the inner swap wins), A refutes it too (the swaps cancel).

assertion: Where two or more material swaps apply to one placed model and the outermost swap does not map a material path the model names, that material is drawn as the model names it: the outermost swap (the reference's, or a SCOL's over its part's) replaces the inner swaps as a whole, and an inner swap's mapping of a path the outer leaves is not applied.
covered_causes: UnsupportedRenderSwapScopes readings differ (draw build, with mswp_outer_scope_wins_v1) where an inner swap maps a material the outermost swap does not map; chained stacks stay refused
origin: No source; weak, and the data points both ways. For it: of the 779 refused placements with a material only an inner scope maps, 14 share their exact position with another placed reference (a separate door, lid or part of the same object); in 5 of them (a boxcar door whose base swaps blue paint to orange over a blue boxcar body, refrigerator door parts over an unswapped body, a forest cliff) the co-located part draws the inner swap's source material unswapped and in none only its target, so the replace reading keeps each object in one colour and the compose reading would not; 2 more show both. Against it: in 418 of the 779 the reference swap maps nothing in the model that the base swap does not map the same way, so under this rule their reference swap only undoes the base's (a reference swap naming building bricks on a boxcar door), which a composition reading would not do; and 46 chained stacks (a reference swap mapping the target of the base's) look written for a sequential application. Chained stacks stay refused.
live_measurement: By an overlay plugin, give one placed model a base swap mapping A to B and D to E and a reference swap mapping only A to C; photograph it: D drawn as D supports it; D drawn as E refutes it (the swaps compose).

assertion: A material swap applied to a placed model leaves a shape whose shader names no material file as it is: the shape is drawn with its own texture set (lighting shader) or source texture (effect shader), as without the swap, while the swap's entries apply to the model's other shapes.
covered_causes: RenderSwapWithoutMaterial (draw build, lighting and effect shapes); the swap's own entries are still read and their refusals stand
origin: Swap entries pair material paths (BNAM and SNAM name .bgsm and .bgem files; swap_census) and the draw build matches them against the material the shader's Name holds; a shape without one offers no key to match. Probe of the 291 bases refused for it in the census before this rule (8,792 placements): every such shape is a lighting or effect shape with a texture of its own beside shapes that do name materials (branches on rock piles, tree bark, an ash layer on debris); where the base has its own swap the model cites every swap source in 4,063 placements, some in 1,575 and none in 162 (a swap that changes no shape); no such shape's own first texture equals the diffuse of a swap's source or target material, so nothing points to a match by texture. Weakness: the game could also hide or retint such a shape; not measured.
live_measurement: Photograph, in one launch, a placed rock pile whose base swaps its ground materials (its branch shape names no material) beside a placement of the unswapped base of the same model: the same branch shape on both supports it; a branch shape changed or absent on the swapped one refutes it.

assertion: A texture file that no mounted archive or loose folder holds, cited only in slots this unlit frame never samples (a material's normal, smooth-specular, environment, glow and other secondary slots; a NIF texture set past its first slot; an effect shader's normal, environment and environment-mask textures, and its greyscale texture where no palette flag is set), leaves the diffuse surface the frame draws as it would be with the file present: the placement is drawn.
covered_causes: MissingTextureUnreadSlot (scene, fo4_scene::missing::unread_textures): a MissingTexture whose every citation in the placement's asset closure is such a slot; a missing texture cited from any slot the frame samples stays MissingTexture
origin: No source. Probe of the 1,074 bases refused for MissingTexture in the census before this rule (one installation): environment maps cited under a cubemap folder that holds none while a file of the same name lies under the shared cubemap folder (three names cited 921 times, about 70 % of the family's area proxy), then smooth-specular, glow and normal maps cited by materials and texture set slots 1, 2 and 4; textures in sampled slots (material diffuse, texture set slot 0, effect source texture) are under a tenth of the family's area. Whether the game draws the rest of a surface unchanged when such a file is absent (or shows a placeholder, or skips the shape) is not established.
live_measurement: Through a loose copy of a placed model's material whose environment map path names an absent file, beside a copy naming an existing cube map, photograph both placements in one launch: the same diffuse colour on both supports it; a placeholder pattern, a missing shape or another base colour refutes it.

assertion: On a lighting-shader surface with blending enabled whose shape sets Shader Flags 2 Vertex_Colors, the alpha that the alpha test and the blend read is the texel alpha times the opacity times the vertex alpha, whether or not Shader Flags 1 Vertex_Alpha is set. The vertex RGB stays out of this unlit frame (render.md), and a lighting surface without blending keeps the frame's policy of no vertex colour.
covered_causes: Draw build (fo4_render::draw, lighting surfaces with a material or a texture set, blended, Vertex_Colors set, a vertex alpha below 1); without the rule such a surface is drawn as before, without vertex alpha
origin: No source: nifxml names the two flags only. Census of every lighting shape with a stored vertex alpha below 1 in the meshes of one installation (actor, LOD and terrain folders left out): 6,891 with Vertex_Colors alone and 6,482 with Vertex_Colors and Vertex_Alpha. On the blended ones the alpha is painted to fade the mesh's open boundary (boundary mean at least 0.25 below the interior's and half its boundary vertices at 0) on 233 of 702 with Vertex_Colors alone and 432 of 986 with both, the pattern of a decal layer faded at its edges; a debris pile's ground layer (36 vertices, alpha 0 to 0.93, Vertex_Colors alone) drew with a hard polygon edge without it. That the lighting shader reads vertex alpha under Vertex_Colors is recognised from prior knowledge, as for effect_vertex_alpha_under_vertex_colors_v1, not from a source: the data shows the alpha is authored, not that the game reads it without Vertex_Alpha.
live_measurement: Photograph, in one launch, a placed debris pile whose blended ground layer fades its vertex alpha to 0 at its edges, beside a loose copy of its NIF whose vertex alpha is set to 1 everywhere (an overlay plugin pointing a copy of the base at it): a soft edge on the shipped model and a hard one on the copy support it; the same hard edge on both refutes it.

assertion: A material swap entry whose BNAM or SNAM path is empty changes nothing: an empty source matches no material a shape names, and an empty target leaves its source as the model names it; the record's other entries apply as they stand.
covered_causes: MaterialSwapEmptyEntry (scene, raised on the swap of a reference or base for each empty BNAM or SNAM path, render only) and the draw build's reading of such an entry; without the rule the empty path stays refused as before (RejectedVfsPath at the scene)
origin: No source. Every winning MSWP of one installation read (names kept outside the repository): 37 BNAM to SNAM pairs in 33 of 3,935 records hold an empty path: 9 pairs with both paths empty (blank rows; identity under any reading that matches paths), 2 with an empty source and 26 with an empty target. The empty targets sit beside filled pairs of the same theme (for example a rock swap whose two other targets are filled), the look of unfinished rows rather than a request to hide a shape; an empty path names no file the game could load. Weakness: the game could treat an empty target as an absent material (a placeholder) or an empty source as matching every shape without a material.
live_measurement: By an overlay plugin, give one placed model two references naming copies of one swap record, one with its empty-target pair removed and one as shipped; photograph both in one launch: identical frames support it; a placeholder, missing or changed shape on the shipped copy refutes it.

assertion: A reference alias filled by a unique actor (ALUA naming an NPC_) holds, while its quest runs and no run set its fill and it has no forced reference (ALFR) or location fill, the one placed actor (a winning, not deleted ACHR in a cell) whose base (NAME) is that NPC_ in the loaded plugins; none or several placed actors leave it without a reference; an alias of the NPC_ the caller names as the player's base (quest_run --player-base, a caller assumption) holds the player. Applied only with quest_run --alias-unique-actors; without it such an alias has no reference, as before.
origin: Prior general knowledge that a unique actor exists once in the world. Measured: of the 2,115 reference aliases whose fill is a unique actor, 1,994 name a base with exactly one placed actor in the loaded plugins, 117 the base the caller names as the player's (which no cell places), 4 a base with none, none a base with several (spec/talk-census.txt, section 7). An actor created or moved by the game, a base placed in a plugin not loaded, and the player's own reference are not settled by anything read.
live_measurement: Start a quest with a unique actor alias in the running game and read the alias's reference from the console (its form id should be the placed actor's); repeat for an alias of the player's base.

assertion: A placed actor (ACHR) stands at its stored DATA position in its cell's space until a native of the run may have moved it (MoveTo, SetPosition and the others the model observes), which leaves its position open, or the caller's assumption (quest_run --assume-actor-at) puts it elsewhere at a second, after which it stands there until another assumption or a later native move. Applied only with quest_run --actor-positions (with --placed-positions and --track); without it an actor's position is open, as before.
origin: Prior general knowledge that an actor starts at its editor placement. No AI package, pathfinding or animation is modelled: an actor that walks in the game is where the caller says. The placed actors of the forced opening's cells: 53 near the track (spec/quest-run-opening.txt).
live_measurement: Read an unmoved placed actor's position from the console (GetPos) after loading its cell in a new game with its AI disabled: it should equal its DATA position.

assertion: When the caller's assumption moves a placed actor (quest_run --assume-actor-at), the trigger volumes of world_trigger_box_v1 and world_trigger_sphere_v1 the actor leaves and enters at that second (point or body reading as for the player) raise OnTriggerLeave and OnTriggerEnter with the actor as the action reference, leaves first, each by volume, under the trigger readings the player's events need (world_trigger_instant_v1, and world_trigger_order_v1 for several at once); a volume holding the actor at its stored position is held without an event. Applied only with quest_run --actor-triggers (with --actor-positions); without it the move raises nothing.
origin: Prior general knowledge that trigger volumes report any actor, the action reference being who entered. The opening's trigger whose handler accepts only one alias's actor (spec/quest-run-opening.txt, section 1) is passed this way. The actor's movement between assumed positions is not modelled: it appears at the assumed position at the assumed second.
live_measurement: In a purpose-built cell, make an NPC walk (by package) into a test trigger whose OnTriggerEnter shows the name of its action reference: the NPC's name supports it.

assertion: A dialogue line's conditions run on the speaker (run-on 0) and on the one spoken to (run-on 1); in a conversation between the player and an actor, a line is tried with the actor speaking to the player and with the player speaking to the actor, function 72 reading the base of the placed actor or the NPC_ the caller names as the player's base (quest_run --player-base). Applied only to lines outside scenes, with quest_run --greeting-on-talk or --hello-lines.
origin: Prior general knowledge of the subject and target of a dialogue condition. Measured: of the 5,987 lines of greeting topics, 212 name the player's base as speaker (run-on 0) and 170 more as speaker with another actor base as listener, 1,705 another actor base as speaker; of the 9,965 lines of hello topics, 174 and 255 name the player's base as speaker, 1,978 another actor base (spec/talk-census.txt, section 4): both parties speak lines of these topics.
live_measurement: In the running game, talk to an actor whose greeting topic holds two test lines, one conditioned on the actor's id as subject and one on the player's: the line heard and its speaker support or reject the reading.

assertion: The line a greeting or hello plays outside a scene is one line of the topics of that subtype (DIAL SNAM) whose owning quest (QNAM) runs: it is known only when exactly one line, with one of the two speakers, has conditions that hold and no other line's are undetermined; otherwise it is undetermined, unless the caller names a line whose conditions hold (quest_run --assume-line, a caller assumption). Applied only with quest_run --greeting-on-talk or --hello-lines.
origin: Prior general knowledge that a topic's lines are chosen by their conditions and that a quest's dialogue is available while it runs. In the forced opening the records never leave a single line: the greeting finds 1,787 lines that hold and 1,788 undetermined among 6,132 candidates of running quests (spec/quest-run-opening.txt).
live_measurement: Not a game behaviour that one test settles alone; refuted by a greeting heard in the running game that this reading would call false or not a candidate (a line of a stopped quest).

assertion: The alternative choice of a line outside a scene: the candidate lines are ordered by their owning quest's priority (DNAM byte 2), then their topic's priority (PNAM), then stored order; the first whose conditions hold plays when every line before it is false; an undetermined line before it leaves the choice undetermined. Applied only with quest_run --dialogue-priority (instead of dialogue_outside_line_choice_v1's single line).
origin: Prior general knowledge that higher-priority quests' dialogue wins. In the forced opening the first candidate by this order is undetermined (a quest of priority 100 whose greeting lines need conditions functions the evaluator does not answer), so the order decides nothing there.
live_measurement: In a test plugin, give two running quests of priorities 10 and 90 a greeting line each for one actor, both holding: the line heard decides between priority and stored order.

assertion: When the player starts a conversation with a placed actor, a line of a greeting topic (SNAM GREE) plays, chosen by dialogue_outside_line_choice_v1 (or dialogue_line_priority_v1); that the player starts a conversation is a caller assumption (quest_run --assume-talk), which also stands for the actor's being there when its enable state is undetermined. Applied only with quest_run --greeting-on-talk.
origin: Prior general knowledge of the subtype code (a game setting's editor id names a Miscellaneous Greeting subtype text, spec/talk-census.txt, section 6). Greeting topics: 476 topics of 5,987 lines, none named by a scene action; 485 of their lines carry a stage field (section 3).
live_measurement: Talk to an actor in the running game whose quest holds a greeting line with a TIQS begin half and read the quest's stages from the console right after: the stage set supports it.

assertion: When the player's track comes within the hello distance of an enabled placed actor standing at its stored position (world_actor_placed_position_v1), a line of a hello topic (SNAM HELO) plays, chosen by dialogue_outside_line_choice_v1 (or dialogue_line_priority_v1); one line per entry within the distance; the distance is the value of the game setting the caller names (quest_run --hello-distance-setting, the setting's choice a caller assumption); the distance is between the reference points. Applied only with quest_run --hello-lines (with --track and --actor-positions).
origin: Prior general knowledge that actors say hello lines to a player who comes near. The setting used in the opening holds 175; a hello timer setting holds 30 s and is not read (no cooldown is modelled). Hello topics: 460 topics of 9,965 lines, none named by a scene action; 495 of their lines carry a stage field (spec/talk-census.txt).
live_measurement: Walk slowly toward an idle actor whose hello topic holds a test line with a notification fragment, reading the distance from the console: the notification at the setting's distance supports it; set the setting to another value and repeat.

assertion: A line played outside a scene by dialogue_greeting_on_talk_v1 or dialogue_hello_proximity_v1 sets the stages of its TIQS (record_set_stage_fields_v1) on its owning quest: the first half as it begins, the second when it ends, its seconds from its voice file for the speaker's voice type (scene_dialogue_line_audio_v1) or the caller's assumed line seconds; a line whose time is not settled sets only its first half. Its script fragments are not run. Applied only with quest_run --line-stage-fields.
origin: As scene_line_stage_fields_v1 for lines outside scenes. Lines outside scenes with a stage field: 1,116 of greeting, hello and other topics no scene action names (spec/talk-census.txt, section 3); 411 lines of greeting, hello and idle topics carry a script block whose fragments are not run (section 5).
live_measurement: As scene_line_stage_fields_v1, for a greeting line: watch the stages as the player talks to the actor.

assertion: The player's handle is not the handle of any record of the loaded plugins: comparing it with a record's handle answers false. Applied only with quest_run --player-no-record; without it the comparison is left open (vm_object_identity_v1).
origin: Measured: no record of the loaded plugins has the player's reference id, and the player's base (as the caller names it) has no placed actor in a cell (spec/talk-census.txt, section 7: the 117 unique actor aliases of that base resolve to no placed actor). A record created at run time for the player is not excluded by anything read.
live_measurement: In a test script, compare Game.GetPlayer() with a placed actor and with a placed marker and show the results: both false support it.

assertion: A placed record below the root of its enable parent chain that carries its own flag 0x800 takes its parent's state through xesp_child_follows_parent_v1 and xesp_flag_bit0_opposite_v1 as any other link: the flag carries no state of its own once the record has an enable parent. Applied only with quest_run --enable-child-flag-ignored (to IsDisabled and the dialogue model's enable checks); without it such a chain is undetermined (xesp_initial_state_chain_v1).
origin: Prior general knowledge that the editor greys out the initially-disabled box of a record with an enable parent; nothing read settles it. In the forced opening the actor of the hello stop carries the flag below an enable parent the run disables, with the opposite bit.
live_measurement: Find a placed record with XESP and its own flag 0x800 whose parent the console can toggle; photograph it with the parent enabled and disabled: presence following the parent supports it; absence in both rejects it.

assertion: ScriptObject.RegisterForAnimationEvent(sender, name) keeps (the calling instance, the sender, the name) until UnregisterForAnimationEvent with that sender and name; an animation event of the sender that the run raises (a caller's --assume-anim-event, or a text key under anim_graph_sequence_keys_v1) runs OnAnimationEvent(sender, name) on every instance registered for that name, in registration order, the handler receiving the name as the registration stored it. Only registered instances receive it (the sender's own scripts without a registration do not). Applied only with quest_run --anim-events; without it the natives are recorded and answered as before.
origin: Prior general knowledge of the engine's animation event registrations, kept as far as anim_event_census section 1 could refute it: 105 compiled scripts call RegisterForAnimationEvent, 111 declare OnAnimationEvent, 98 do both; the opening's handlers compare the sender and the name and unregister after handling. Whether a registration survives the sender's 3D unloading (the OnAnimationEventUnregistered event the scripts declare) is not modelled.
live_measurement: Attach a test script to a quest that registers for a named event of a placed activator and shows a message in OnAnimationEvent; play the activator's animation so that the event fires twice: two messages support the registration lasting until it is removed; one refutes it.
reason: Behaviour of the running game not measured; the opening's 505, 515 and 530 depend on it.

assertion: Animation event names compare ignoring ASCII case: a registration matches an event of the same name in another case, and a graph event matches its graph's event table in another case (crate::anim); the handler receives the registration's spelling. Applied only with quest_run --anim-event-case; without it names must be equal byte for byte.
origin: Prior general knowledge that the engine's event names are case-insensitive strings, kept because anim_event_census section 2 finds 5 registered names only in another case in NIF text keys and 4 in behaviour graph event tables (in the opening, one registration against an elevator's key and one PlayAnimation argument against a graph event, each differing only in case).
live_measurement: Register a test script for an event in another case than the NIF text key that raises it, play the sequence: a delivered event supports it; none refutes it.
reason: Behaviour of the running game not measured; the opening's 530 depends on it.

assertion: A placed reference runs the behaviour graph its base model names (the BSBehaviorGraphExtraData file under meshes, its project's one character file, that character's behaviour file, both relative to the project's folder; fo4_scene::anim_graph), from the root state machine's start state (the i32 at +168) when the run first plays an animation on it, none of the start state's text keys raised; ObjectReference.PlayAnimation(event), and a text key raised under anim_graph_sequence_keys_v1, takes the current state's transition whose event (the i32 at +48 of the 72-byte element) names that event, else a wildcard transition of the machine (local before wildcard), entering the target state (the i32 at +52) at once (the transition effect's duration not read); a transition with a condition (+40) or to a state the machine does not hold leaves the graph undetermined from then on. Applied only with quest_run --anim-graphs; without it PlayAnimation is recorded as before.
origin: The file chain and the offsets are measured over the installation (anim_event_census sections 4 and 5: 450 behaviour graphs read; start state among the state ids in 449; every transition's event within the event table and target among the state ids, 1,775 local and 954 wildcard; 321 of 342 project files resolve their character and graph; 1,176 of 1,189 NIFs naming a graph file name a project file). That a graph starts in its start state, how transitions are chosen and that they take no time are prior general knowledge, as is that PlayAnimation sends a graph event; the words at +56 to +72 of a transition are not read.
live_measurement: Play an animation event on a placed activator whose graph has a wildcard and a local transition on the same event, and photograph which sequence plays; time from PlayAnimation to the first visible motion against the sequence's first key.
reason: Behaviour of the running game not measured; the opening's 505, 515 and 530 depend on it.

assertion: A graph state whose generator is a BGSGamebryoSequenceGenerator plays the model's NIF controller sequence its name (the text at +136) names from the sequence's start: each text key whose text is an event of the graph is raised at the state's entry plus (key time - start time) / frequency, in time order, as an animation event of the reference (vm_anim_event_registration_v1) and as an event of its graph (anim_graph_model_transition_v1); leaving the state drops the keys not yet raised; the keys of a sequence are raised once per entry (a looping sequence's later passes are not raised). Applied only with quest_run --anim-graph-keys (with --anim-graphs).
origin: Prior general knowledge that Gamebryo text keys become behaviour events; the census (anim_event_census section 2) finds 18 registered names as exact NIF text keys and 125 in graph event tables; in the opening one key of an activator's sequence (3.47 s) and two keys of an elevator's sequence (6.57 s and 7.53 s) are what the scripts wait on. Timing against the real clock, blending and cycle types other than the stored 2 are not measured.
live_measurement: With a test script registered for two keys of one sequence, log Utility.GetCurrentRealTime() at PlayAnimation and at each OnAnimationEvent: differences equal to the key times over the frequency support it.
reason: Behaviour of the running game not measured; the opening's 505, 515 and 530 depend on it.

assertion: A scene action of kind 1 whose package (PNAM) holds exactly one Location data input (PLDT) whose word names a placed reference (REFR or ACHR) puts the actor its alias holds in the run at that reference's stored position N seconds after the action starts, N the caller's (quest_run --package-destinations N): an assumed actor move of the world model (world_actor_placed_position_v1, world_actor_trigger_v1), no path and no speed; a move not yet applied when its scene stops is dropped. Packages with no or several such inputs move no one. Applied only with --package-destinations; without it no package moves anyone.
origin: The PACK layout is measured (package_census: 4,888 of 4,888 read; PKCU count equals the inputs in all; PLDT kind 0 names a REFR in 2,097 and an ACHR in 15); that the Location input is where the package takes the actor, and that the actor gets there, are prior general knowledge; 1,035 of 3,292 scene package actions have exactly one such input.
live_measurement: Start a scene whose package action travels an actor to a marker inside a test trigger that shows a message: the message, and its delay against the actor's distance and speed, support the destination and calibrate N.
reason: Behaviour of the running game not measured; with it five of the seven actor moves the talk step assumed come from the data.

assertion: A material swap source (BNAM) holding `*` is a pattern over the material path a shape's shader names, both compared as resolved keys (lower case, `/` separators, the materials root): each `*` stands for any run of characters, possibly empty, separators included. The pair's target (SNAM) is taken as it is when it holds no `*`, and with each `*` replaced, in order, by the run the source's `*` matched when it holds as many; a path the pattern splits in more than one way with different targets, or a target with another count of `*`, is refused (AmbiguousMaterialSwap, UnsupportedSwapPattern).
covered_causes: The draw build's reading of BNAM paths holding `*` (fo4_render::draw, fo4_scene::swap_pattern) and the scene's loading of the targets they give, done only where the rule may be relied on (the hypotheses level); without the rule such a source compares as bytes and matches no material, as before
origin: No source. Every winning MSWP of one installation read (names kept outside the repository): 68 of 3,935 records hold `*`, in 131 BNAM to SNAM pairs, almost all rock and ground swaps of landscape regions. Over the placed references: 34,509 placements sit under a swap scope holding a pattern, and in 12,939 of them a pattern matches a material their models name. Where source and target both hold one `*` (or two), 20 of the 24 targets formed for placed materials name a file an archive holds (for example a rubble rock decal formed into a coastal sand decal), files a byte comparison never reaches; for patterns into a plain target, 83 of 84 targets exist, leaving aside one record whose bare `*` maps every material to a test material no archive holds. Weakness: that `*` is a pattern at all, that it may match an empty run and cross separators, that matching ignores case like every path here, and that target stars are filled in order are prior general knowledge of file patterns, read back from the data only by the formed targets that exist; the game could also ignore such entries, as the byte comparison does.
live_measurement: By an overlay plugin, place two copies of one rock model whose material a coastal swap's pattern matches, the first naming the shipped swap and the second a copy whose pattern pair is replaced by the literal pair it forms for that material; photograph both in one launch: identical frames support it; the first copy keeping the model's own material while the second changes refutes it.

assertion: Where a literal BNAM and a pattern BNAM of one swap both match the material a shape names and give different targets, the literal entry's target is drawn, whatever their order in the record.
covered_causes: The draw build's choice between such entries (fo4_render::draw); the scene loads no pattern target for a material a literal source of the same swap maps
origin: No source. In the 68 swap records holding `*`, a literal source falls under a pattern of the same record 15 times, always with a different target: 11 times the literal entry comes first, 4 times the pattern does. One literal entry maps a material to itself, pointless unless it is meant as an exception to the pattern beside it; the others map a trim material to a trim target beside a pattern mapping the general material, and in one record the pattern's target is a distant-LOD material while the literal one is a full-detail trim. 2,772 placements meet such a pair on a material their models name. Weakness: an argument from authoring intent, not a measurement; the game could apply the first matching entry, which differs on the 4 records whose pattern comes first.
live_measurement: On a coastal cliff placement whose swap lists the pattern before the literal trim entry, photograph the trim faces: the literal entry's trim target supports it; the pattern's target (a distant-LOD material) refutes it in favour of record order.

assertion: A pattern pair whose target, as formed for a material (the one a shape names, or one another swap of the placement puts in its place), is a file no archive holds changes nothing for that material: it stays as it was before that pair.
covered_causes: MissingSwapPatternTarget (scene, raised on the swap for each such target, render only, for the materials the models under the swap name and the targets the placement's swaps put in place; the target is kept out of the instance's assets) and the draw build's reading of such a pair (fo4_render::draw); without the rule the pair is refused
origin: No source. One swap record whose source is a bare `*` maps every material to a test material no archive holds; it is named by 3,619 placed references of finished content (roof and cliff kits), whose models would otherwise lose every material. Besides it, 5 targets formed from patterns for placed materials name no file (decal variants of ground materials whose plain variants exist), as a pattern written over a family of materials meets members without a counterpart. Weakness: the game could draw such a shape with a missing-material placeholder, hide it, or apply the pair's other readings; nothing here was seen in the running game.
live_measurement: Photograph, in one launch, a placed roof piece named by the bare-`*` swap beside an unswapped placement of the same model: identical surfaces support it; a placeholder or missing surface on the swapped copy refutes it.

assertion: Where two or more swap scopes apply to one placed model and one scope maps the material another scope put in place (a chain), the material is found by following the chain: starting from the path the model names, the outermost scope not yet applied that maps the current material applies, and so on, each scope at most once.
covered_causes: The draw build's reading of swap scopes whose four readings differ and that form a chain (fo4_render::draw, settle); without the rule they stay refused (UnsupportedRenderSwapScopes readings differ, chained)
origin: No source. The 94 placements refused for chained scopes alone (shard census of one installation, names kept outside the repository): in most, the base's swap maps a rock or ground material to a regional variant and the reference's swap maps that variant again (for example a cliff material to its wet version), while it does not map the model's own material: a swap written against another swap's targets, which only a reading that applies both in turn can use. Where both scopes map the model's material, the outer target is mapped again by the inner swap in the quarry floors (marble to rough to dirty rough). Weakness: it is a reading of authoring intent; it sits beside mswp_outer_scope_replaces_v1, under which an outer swap that does not map a material leaves the inner one out, so the two together say an outer swap replaces the inner one except where it maps the inner one's targets; a single order of application could explain the chains and not the co-located cases that support replacement.
live_measurement: On a coastal rock placement whose base swap maps a boulder material to a cliff material and whose reference swap maps that cliff material to its wet version, photograph the rock beside an unswapped copy of the base: the wet cliff material supports it; the boulder material (outer replaces) or the dry cliff material (inner only) refutes it.

assertion: A triangle of a NIF shape that uses a vertex whose texture coordinate is not a finite number is not drawn; the shape's other triangles are drawn as usual.
covered_causes: RenderNonFiniteVertex raised for a texture coordinate (fo4_render::draw); positions that are not finite stay refused
origin: No source. Every model of the 683 placements refused for non-finite vertices alone read (names kept outside the repository): the non-finite values are always texture coordinates, both components NaN, never positions; 3 to 52 vertices of shapes of hundreds or thousands (building siding, door frames, ground frames), every one used by a triangle; none of those triangles is degenerate, and they cover at most 2.8 % of their shape's area (mostly below 0.5 %); most of the vertices share their position with a vertex whose coordinate is finite, as seam duplicates do. Weakness: a GPU samples a NaN coordinate in a way this project does not know; the game could draw those slivers with some texel instead of leaving them out.
live_measurement: Photograph, close and in one launch, the faces of a door frame model that holds such triangles: a hole or a missing sliver where they lie supports it; a continuous textured surface refutes it (then the triangles are drawn with some texel).

assertion: A placed reference's primitive (XPRM: three bound words, three colour words, a float and a kind word) draws nothing and adds nothing to the reference's collision; the base is drawn, and its collision placed, as for a reference without it.
covered_causes: RuntimeRecordState REFR.XPRM (render and collision readiness), raised once the layout table holds the measured 32-byte layout
origin: No source for what it shows; the layout is measured (world_census: 32 bytes on all 30,028 placed references with one, colour words and word 6 in 0 to 1, kind words 1 to 5). By base: 10,979 texture sets, 1,269 acoustic spaces and 642 sounds (outside this frame), 7,131 activators of which 6,981 have no model, 9,356 statics without a model (light boxes, collision, room, portal and plane markers, clip volumes), 14 containers, doors and furniture, and 637 statics with a model, 636 of them ordinary (buildings, road pieces, trees, fences) whose references carry nothing else unusual; 2,513 placements were omitted for XPRM alone. The colour words suggest an editor display colour; no field links the primitive to the base's model. Weakness: whether a primitive shows in play (as a volume, an occluder, a collision box) is not settled by any field; the rule rests on the absence of any link to the model.
live_measurement: Photograph, in one launch, a placed building whose reference carries a primitive beside an overlay copy of the same reference without it, and walk into both: identical frames and the same collision support it; a visible volume, a missing building or a different collision refutes it.

assertion: ObjectReference.MoveTo(target, x, y, z, ...) with the three offsets zero puts the receiver at the target's position, in the target's space (its interior cell or worldspace), at the second of the call, when the world model settles the target's position (a placed reference at its stored position, or one this rule already placed); the receiver's position then reads that place (crate::track, placed_at) until a later native moves it or a caller's or a package's later move does. A non-zero offset, or a target whose position is open, leaves the receiver's position open as before. Applied only with quest_run --moveto-target (with --track); without it every moved reference's position is open.
origin: Prior general knowledge of MoveTo's arguments (the target, offsets along the world axes, the match-rotation flag); the run's MoveTo calls in the forced opening all pass three float zeros. Nothing read settles whether the move takes effect at once, whether the receiver is placed on the target's reference point or on the ground or the navigation mesh near it, or its facing.
live_measurement: In a test cell, MoveTo a placed actor to a marker from a script and log GetPositionX/Y/Z and GetParentCell right after the call and a second later: the marker's position and cell at once support it; a later or offset position refutes it.
reason: Behaviour of the running game not measured; the load step's opening places three actors in an interior by it.

assertion: A placed reference that comes into the interior cell the player's track is in, moved there by a native (MoveTo, SetPosition, MoveToNode, MoveToMyEditorLocation, TranslateTo) or enabled there (Enable), and is enabled in the run, has its 3D loaded at once: OnLoad runs on its own scripts, on the scripts of the quest aliases holding it and on the instances registered for the remote event, as a caller's --assume-load delivers it (crate::load, crate::player). A reference loads once until the player's area leaves it; OnUnload, OnCellLoad, OnCellAttach and OnCellDetach are not raised; a reference whose enable state is undetermined does not load (counted). Applied only with quest_run --load-in-cell (with --track); without it no load is raised.
origin: Prior general knowledge that a reference's 3D loads when it is in a loaded cell and that OnLoad then runs; kept as far as load_census could refute it (spec/load-event-census.txt): 402 compiled scripts declare OnLoad with code, 54 of the handlers sit in the script's auto state (a script waiting for its load), 25 handlers register for animation events and 33 for remote events, 51 call Is3DLoaded; 81 quest alias scripts with OnLoad sit on unique actor aliases. The order against the stage fragment that moved the reference (after its jobs) and that the load takes no time are assumptions.
live_measurement: Attach a test script with OnLoad that shows the real time to an actor in another cell; MoveTo it to the player from the console: a message at once supports it; none, or one only after the player leaves and re-enters the cell, refutes it.
reason: Behaviour of the running game not measured; the opening's 644, 645 and 646 depend on it (their handlers register only in OnLoad).

assertion: When the player's track reaches an interior cell (a point of the track in a new space: the instant load through a door, the caller's track), every enabled placed reference standing in that cell whose own record or base carries a VMAD, and every reference the running quests' aliases hold that stands there, has its 3D loaded at that second, OnLoad delivered as under world_load_reference_enters_v1, in record key order (the alias-held references after the cell's own). Applied only with quest_run --load-on-arrival (with --track); without it no load is raised on arrival.
origin: Prior general knowledge that a door's load brings the destination cell's references into memory before the player can act; load_census finds 2,977 attachments of a script with OnLoad on placed references of interior cells (84 of them on initially disabled references). That the loads happen at the track's arrival second, all before the trigger events of that second, and in record key order, is an assumption with no source.
live_measurement: In a test interior, place two references with OnLoad scripts that log the real time and the order; walk through a load door: both logged at the arrival support the second; the logged order against their form ids supports or refutes the order.
reason: Behaviour of the running game not measured; in the load step's opening it raises the loads of the vault's own scripted references and changes no stage.

assertion: In a worldspace, a placed reference whose position lies within N exterior grid squares (4,096 units, world_census) of the player's square on both axes, N the caller's (quest_run --load-grid N), has its 3D loaded when the player's square changes so that it comes within range, or when a native moves or enables it within range; the candidates are the scripted references of the cells of those squares (the worldspace's cells without a square filtered by position), the references the running quests' aliases hold and the objects natives moved or enabled; OnLoad delivered as under world_load_reference_enters_v1. Applied only with quest_run --load-grid N (with --track); without it no exterior load is raised.
origin: Prior general knowledge of a loaded grid of exterior cells around the player whose size is an engine setting not stored in the plugins (hence the caller's N); load_census finds 3,783 attachments of a script with OnLoad on placed references of exterior cells. Whether references load by cell or by distance, and the setting's value, are not settled by any record read.
live_measurement: Place a test activator with an OnLoad script that logs, N + 1 cells from the player, and walk toward it logging the player's position at the message: the square where it fires gives N.
reason: Behaviour of the running game not measured; not used by the load step's final run.

assertion: Condition function 131 is how far, in percent, the action of the scene its first parameter names, with the index (INAM) its second parameter gives, has run on the scene clock (scene_clock_v1): 0 before the action starts (and when the scene is not playing), 100 once it completed, and for a running action the clock times (a timer's seconds, a line's audio or the caller's seconds for a line) 100 times the seconds since it started over its seconds; a running action the clock does not time is undetermined. A scene whose completion conditions are false and hold such a condition on a running timed action is offered them again at the second the share reaches the comparison value. Applied only with quest_run --cond-131-clock (with --scene-clock); without it the function is not evaluated, and --assume-cond 131=VALUE remains the alternative.
origin: The meaning was recognised from prior knowledge (no public table of function indexes was read) and kept because action_percent_census could refute it and did not (spec/action-percent-census.txt): all 52 conditions sit in scene phase completion lists, all with operator 3 (at least) and an integer value from 1 to 99, the first parameter always the host scene itself, the second always the index of exactly one of its actions, a dialogue line (39), a response line (12) or player dialogue (1), the action ending in that phase in 48 of 52. That the share is linear in time, and that 0 and 100 bound it, are assumptions.
live_measurement: In a test scene, give a phase a completion condition of function 131 on its own dialogue action at 50, with a long line, and log the real time at the phase's end fragment against the line's start and its audio length: half the length supports it.
reason: Behaviour of the running game not measured; the opening's vault scene and two earlier scenes wait on it (with --phase-conditions-end, on the share; without, the phase still waits for its action).

assertion: A scene phase whose completion list is not empty ends as soon as the list holds, its timed actions still running (they keep their due seconds but hold no later phase); a phase with an empty list still waits for its actions (scene_clock_v1). The list is offered again at each action's completion and at the seconds function 131 conditions reach their values (cond_fn_131_action_percent_v1). Applied only with quest_run --phase-conditions-end (with --scene-clock); without it a phase waits for every action spanning it, then reads its completion conditions, as before.
origin: Prior general knowledge of the editor's phase completion conditions; the census of function 131 (every one on an action of the same scene, 47 of 52 on an action that starts and ends in that phase, at 1 to 99 percent) only makes sense if the condition can end the phase before its action does. Whether a running line is cut, kept or overlapped by the next phase's line is not settled.
live_measurement: Time the start of the next phase's line in a scene whose phase completes on function 131 at 50 of a long line: a start at half the line, with the first line still audible, supports it; a start only after the line ends refutes it.
reason: Behaviour of the running game not measured; with it the opening's vault scene ends its phases earlier (the same stages are reached).
