assertion: A controller with the Active flag, played forwards (Play Backwards clear), of Anim Type APP_TIME, not run by a manager (Manager Controlled clear where the model has a NiControllerManager) and named by no NiControllerSequence starts when its model loads and runs on the game clock: s seconds after the load its controller time is Start Time + Phase + Frequency x s, folded into Start Time to Stop Time by its cycle type (nif_controller_cycle_loop_v1, _reverse_v1, _clamp_v1), and its one keyframe interpolator (NiFloatInterpolator with NiFloatData) gives the value of its keys at that time (nif_key_linear_v1, nif_key_quadratic_hermite_v1, nif_key_constant_step_v1), which replaces the driven shader field. The frame takes it for the alpha and the UV offset and scale components of effect shaders (EffectShaderControlledVariable 5 to 9) and lighting shaders (LightingShaderControlledFloat 12, 20 to 23). At s = 0 it gives the key at Start Time, on which every such track's first key sits: it agrees with nif_controller_rest_effect_first_key_v1 and nif_controller_rest_texture_first_key_v1 wherever they settle a field (stored value = first key), and where the stored value is not the first key (those rules leave the model refused) the clock never draws the stored value. Where a BGEM holds a value of the field other than the NIF's, effect_material_over_controller_v1 keeps the material's value at every time and the clock does not drive that field (the two rules would otherwise contradict: one says the material replaces the field, this one that the controller does); a lighting material that differs is refused (UnsettledClockMaterialField). Controllers run by a manager's sequences do not advance on this clock (nif_controller_rest_manager_idle_v1, nif_controller_rest_loop_unstarted_v1).
covered_causes: UnsupportedAnimationRuntime ...;rest=clock (the controller, its NiFloatInterpolator and NiFloatData); the draw build with a time (fo4_render::draw::BuildOptions::time; render --time, fo4-view --clock): the draw's UV offset, UV scale and opacity and DrawList::animations; without a time the instance is omitted (UnsettledControllerTime)
origin: controller_census (spec/controller-census.txt, Clock; spec/controller-clock.md): of 2,999 free-running alpha and UV controllers of effect and lighting shaders, 2,886 are active with APP_TIME and not played backwards and 113 inactive with APP_INIT (left out); frequency 1 and phase 0 on every one; 2,346 give a track (left out: zero or negative span 496, inactive 113, TBC keys 44); on every track the first key sits on Start Time and the last on Stop Time; the stored field equals the clock's value at load on 1,937 tracks and lies inside the key range, away from it, on the other 409 (never outside the range); 1,226 looping UV offsets step by a whole number at the seam and 856 tracks end on their first value. That a free-running controller runs from its model's load on the game clock, and the time formula, are recognised from prior knowledge of Gamebryo controllers; nifxml names the fields (Frequency 'usually 1.0', Phase 'usually 0.0', Start Time, Stop Time, TimeControllerFlags) but gives no formula.
live_measurement: Load a cell with a placed scrolling effect (a waterfall or smoke card whose V offset a free-running looping controller drives, span known from the NIF) and record frames from the moment the loading screen ends over a few cycles: the offset at frame time t must follow Start Time + t folded by the span; an offset still at load, one that starts later than the load, or a period other than the span over the frequency refutes it. Reloading the cell must restart it at the first key; an offset that continues from where it was supports the game's absolute clock instead.

assertion: A controller the clock runs with cycle type 0 (CYCLE_LOOP in TimeControllerFlags bits 1 and 2) wraps its time into Start Time to Stop Time: Start Time + ((t - Start Time) modulo (Stop Time - Start Time)); at the seam the value goes from the key at Stop Time back to the key at Start Time at once.
covered_causes: UnsupportedAnimationRuntime ...;rest=clock-loop; the draw build with a time
origin: nifxml CycleType names LOOP, without a formula. controller_census: 2,150 of the 2,346 alpha and UV tracks loop; 1,226 looping UV offsets step by a whole number at the seam (a texture that scrolls by whole repeats, seamless under a wrap) and 856 tracks end on their first value. The modulo is prior knowledge.
live_measurement: Record two full cycles of a looping UV-scroll effect: a period of (Stop Time - Start Time) / Frequency and a jump back (not a reversal) at the seam support it; motion back and forth refutes it.

assertion: A controller the clock runs with cycle type 1 (CYCLE_REVERSE) goes from Start Time to Stop Time and back, period 2 x (Stop Time - Start Time): with u = (t - Start Time) modulo twice the span, its time is Start Time + u while u is at most the span and Start Time + 2 x span - u after.
covered_causes: UnsupportedAnimationRuntime ...;rest=clock-reverse; the draw build with a time
origin: nifxml CycleType names REVERSE, without a formula. controller_census: no alpha or UV track has it (8 free-running transform controllers do); registered because the clock code names this reading. The back-and-forth reading is prior knowledge.
live_measurement: On a model with a reverse-cycle controller (none among the alpha and UV tracks; a test copy of a looping UV effect with the cycle bits set to 1 by an overlay), record two periods: the offset must run forward over one span and back over the next.

assertion: A controller the clock runs with cycle type 2 (CYCLE_CLAMP) holds its time between Start Time and Stop Time: before Start Time the key at Start Time, after Stop Time the key at Stop Time, which then stays.
covered_causes: UnsupportedAnimationRuntime ...;rest=clock-clamp; the draw build with a time
origin: nifxml CycleType names CLAMP (the default of TimeControllerFlags), without a formula. controller_census: 196 of the 2,346 alpha and UV tracks are clamped (102 quadratic, 90 linear, 4 constant keys). Holding the last key is prior knowledge.
live_measurement: Record a clamped alpha fade of a free-running controller from the load past its Stop Time: the alpha must stop changing at Stop Time and keep the last key's value; a repeat refutes it.

assertion: Between two keys of a LINEAR_KEY (1) group the value is linear in the key time; before the first key the value is the first key's, after the last key the last key's; keys with equal times give the later key's value.
covered_causes: UnsupportedAnimationRuntime ...;rest=clock-linear; the draw build with a time
origin: nifxml KeyType: 'Use linear interpolation.' Holding the end keys outside them is prior knowledge (the clock's time never leaves the first and last key on the census's tracks, which sit on Start Time and Stop Time). controller_census: 586 alpha and UV tracks.
live_measurement: Record frames at a quarter, half and three quarters of an interval of a linear UV scroll (a two-key loop): offsets in equal steps support it; an eased curve refutes it.

assertion: Between two keys of a QUADRATIC_KEY (2) group the value is the cubic Hermite curve through the two values whose slopes are the first key's Forward Tangent and the second key's Backward Tangent, taken per interval: with s = (t - t0) / (t1 - t0), value = (2s^3 - 3s^2 + 1) v0 + (s^3 - 2s^2 + s) F0 + (-2s^3 + 3s^2) v1 + (s^3 - s^2) B1, the tangents not divided by the interval's length; the end keys' values outside them as for linear keys.
covered_causes: UnsupportedAnimationRuntime ...;rest=clock-quadratic; the draw build with a time (and the opacity bounds the build checks)
origin: nifxml KeyType: 'Use quadratic interpolation. Forward and back tangents will be stored.' The curve with two end values and two end slopes is a cubic (Hermite), from prior knowledge, whatever the enum's name. controller_census: 1,747 alpha and UV tracks. Of 13,330 intervals of the free-running float tracks whose time step is not 1 and whose value changes, 10,011 have a zero forward tangent (both scalings of the tangent agree), 361 a tangent equal to the interval's difference (the per-interval scaling of a straight line), 246 equal to the difference per second, 2,712 neither: the tangent's scale is not settled by the data.
live_measurement: Record many frames inside one interval of a quadratic alpha pulse whose tangents are not zero and whose interval is not 1 second long: compare the brightness against the Hermite curve with tangents per interval and per second; a straight line between the keys refutes the curve itself.

assertion: In a CONST_KEY (5) group the value is that of the last key at or before the time (a step), the first key's before it.
covered_causes: UnsupportedAnimationRuntime ...;rest=clock-step; the draw build with a time
origin: nifxml KeyType: 'Step function. Used for visibility keys in NiBoolData.' controller_census: 13 alpha and UV tracks have constant keys.
live_measurement: Record a UV track with constant keys (a frame-by-frame flipbook offset) at times between two keys: the offset of the earlier key supports it; an offset between the two refutes it.

assertion: A looping NiControllerSequence (cycle type 0) of a NiControllerManager is not started by its model's loading or by the game clock: where nothing starts it (no behaviour graph, whose models stay refused as behavior-graph, and no script, whose references stay refused as VMAD), its controlled blocks other than effect-shader controllers (which keep effect-idle) and what their interpolators reach leave the model's fields and node transforms as stored, at load and at every time of the clock. Tension: nif_controller_rest_effect_first_key_v1 and nif_controller_rest_texture_first_key_v1 read a looping sequence as showing its first key at the frame's instant and settle it only where the stored field is that key, so the two readings agree there; this rule draws the stored field where they differ, which means the instant those rules name is a sequence that never started. A looping sequence that the engine starts by itself on load (an ambient loop) would refute this rule while those two could still hold at load.
covered_causes: UnsupportedAnimationRuntime ...;rest=manager-loop (a looping NiControllerSequence and the interpolators and data its controlled blocks reach); render and collision readiness
origin: controller_census (spec/controller-census.txt, Clock and manager-loop): 550 models carry the tag (11,640 placements); 104 of them (1,370 placements) have no other open tag and are decided by this rule; of the tagged models with a placement, 71 are named only by movable statics, 66 only by activators and 34 only by statics; 54 hold a single looping sequence and no behaviour graph. That a manager's sequences are started by name (by a behaviour graph or a script) is prior knowledge, as for nif_controller_rest_manager_idle_v1; that the engine never starts a looping sequence by itself is the claim under test and the census cannot weigh it.
live_measurement: Photograph over several seconds, without interacting, a placed movable static whose manager has one looping sequence and no behaviour graph and whose reference and base have no script (a fan or a turning sign): no motion supports it; a moving part refutes it (the sequence starts on load).

live_measurement: Record frames from the end of a loading screen of a placed model whose part a free-running looping translation controller moves (a swinging or sliding part with no script): the part's position over time should follow the keys at Start Time + s folded by the cycle; a part that stays at its stored position, or moves with another period, refutes it.

assertion: With its switch on (--clock-rotation; fo4_scene::clock::Switches::rotation; off by default), the rotation of a node a free-running transform controller moves (as nif_clock_transform_translation_v1) is, s seconds after load, read from the NiTransformData's quaternion rotation keys at the controller's time: between two linear keys their spherical linear interpolation along the shorter arc, normalised (fo4_scene::clock::slerp); between two step keys the earlier key (nif_key_constant_step_v1); the first key's before the first and the last key's after the last; the quaternion (w, x, y, z) turned into rotation words as rest::quaternion_rows. Without rotation keys the interpolator's pose quaternion where set, else the stored words. Quadratic and TBC quaternion keys have no reading here.
covered_causes: UnsupportedAnimationRuntime ...;rest=clock-rotation, given only with the switch on; draw build instances with a moving node
origin: motion_census: quaternion rotation keys vary on 766 free-running tracks, all of key type linear (no quadratic or TBC quaternion keys occur); consecutive keys always lie in one hemisphere (the shorter-arc choice changes nothing in the data); the largest step between consecutive keys is 10 to 90 degrees on most tracks, where slerp, normalised linear and componentwise linear interpolation differ visibly; the key at load equals the stored rotation words under rest::quaternion_rows on 608 of 769 tracks. Slerp itself is prior knowledge. Weak.
live_measurement: Watch a placed model whose part a free-running quaternion-key controller turns by a large step between two keys (45 to 90 degrees): at the middle of the interval the part should be at half the angle about one fixed axis; a part that speeds up and slows down within the interval (normalised linear interpolation) or leaves the axis refutes it.

assertion: With its switch on (--clock-rotation-xyz; fo4_scene::clock::Switches::rotation_xyz; off by default), the rotation of a node a free-running transform controller moves (as nif_clock_transform_translation_v1) whose NiTransformData stores Rotation Type XYZ is, s seconds after load, read from its three float key groups at the controller's time, each angle by its key rule (nif_key_linear_v1, nif_key_quadratic_hermite_v1, nif_key_constant_step_v1) and read in radians, then composed as the rotation about X applied first to a child point, then about Y, then about Z (rows Rz * Ry * Rx acting on column vectors, each counter-clockwise looking down its axis; fo4_scene::clock::XYZ_ORDER). An empty angle group, or TBC keys, has no reading.
covered_causes: UnsupportedAnimationRuntime ...;rest=clock-rotation-xyz, given only with the switch on; draw build instances with a moving node
origin: motion_census: XYZ angle keys vary on 628 free-running tracks (each axis linear, quadratic or step; TBC on 85, which stay refused). Of the 24 readings of the angles at load (6 axis orders, 2 signs, radians or degrees), where two or three angles turn, 'radians, X then Y then Z, counter-clockwise' is the only reading that gives the node's stored rotation words on 84 tracks and is among the matching readings on every one of the 208 tracks that some reading matches (8 match none); degrees never single one out. Those tracks have few placements. Interpolating each angle apart before composing is prior knowledge. Medium for the order and unit at load, weak between keys.
live_measurement: Watch a placed model whose part an XYZ-key controller turns about two axes at once: the part's orientation at a few times should equal Rz * Ry * Rx of the keys' angles at those times; another order, or a part turning about a single fixed axis between keys, refutes it.

assertion: With its switch on (--clock-scale; fo4_scene::clock::Switches::scale; off by default), the uniform scale of a node a free-running transform controller moves (as nif_clock_transform_translation_v1) is, s seconds after load, the value of its NiTransformData scale keys at the controller's time by the key rules, or without scale keys the interpolator's pose scale where set and the stored scale otherwise. A world scale that is not positive is refused (ClockTrackValue).
covered_causes: UnsupportedAnimationRuntime ...;rest=clock-scale, given only with the switch on; draw build instances with a moving node
origin: motion_census: scale keys vary on 131 free-running tracks (linear 104, quadratic 21, TBC 6 which stay refused); the scale at load equals the stored scale on 351 of 357 keyed tracks. That the keys replace the node's scale is the prior knowledge of the translation rule. Weak.
live_measurement: Watch a placed model whose part a free-running scale controller grows or shrinks (a pulsing part): its size over time should follow the keys at Start Time + s folded by the cycle; a constant size refutes it.

assertion: A script's ObjectReference.Activate(actor, false) (default processing with events) on a placed furniture reference the run does not have that actor sitting in, the actor the player's handle or a placed actor, makes that actor sit in the furniture at once, as vm_furniture_activate_sits_v1 reads the default-processing-only activation: the sit is delivered under vm_event_sit_v1 after the calling job. The furniture's own OnActivate is not delivered (a script's activation raising events is not modelled; counted). Applied only with quest_run --activate-furniture-events (with --sit-events); without it an activation with events sits no one, as before.
origin: Prior general knowledge that a furniture's default activation by an actor makes the actor use it whether or not the activation's events are also raised. Data: the opening's sequence quest stage fragment that moves the player to the postwar vault activates the player's postwar cryopod for the player with false and plays the furniture graph's instant-occupied wildcard event on it in the next call; the next main quest's exit scene later activates the same pod for the player with false again, and the pod's graph then needs a get-up event to open (anim_furniture_sit_graph_events_v1). Weakness: whether the engine sits an actor through a scripted activation with events, and with what delay, is not in the data; OnActivate is left out.
live_measurement: From a test script, call Activate(Game.GetPlayer(), false) on a chair and log OnSit on a player alias and OnActivate on the chair with the real time: both (and the delay) support it; no OnSit refutes it.
reason: Behaviour of the running game not measured; the exit step relies on it in the forced opening.

assertion: A script's ObjectReference.Activate(actor, true or false) on the placed furniture reference the run has that actor sitting in makes the actor get up from it: the get-up is delivered under vm_event_sit_v1 (OnGetUp to the sitter's receivers, OnExitFurniture to the furniture's) after the calling job, before the sits the same job brought. An undetermined second argument reads nothing (counted). Applied only with quest_run --activate-furniture-get-up (with --sit-events); without it such an activation is read as before (a sit in the same furniture changes nothing).
origin: Prior general knowledge that activating the furniture one sits in stands one up. Data: the next main quest's exit scene begins its third phase with a stage whose fragment activates the player's pod for the player while the run has the player sitting in it (from vm_furniture_activate_events_sits_v1), and the pod's behaviour graph holds, in the state the earlier wildcard event left it in, a transition on an event its other occupied states also take toward the exit state whose sequence carries the key the exit scene's fragment registered for. Weakness: whether a scripted activation by the sitter stands it up, and when, is not in the data; the sitter's animation is not modelled.
live_measurement: Sit the player in a chair, then from a test script call Activate(Game.GetPlayer(), false) on it and log OnGetUp on a player alias with the real time: an OnGetUp supports it; none refutes it.
reason: Behaviour of the running game not measured; the exit step relies on it in the forced opening.

assertion: A sit or a get-up that a script's activation brings (vm_furniture_activate_sits_v1, vm_furniture_activate_events_sits_v1, vm_furniture_activate_get_up_v1) sends the furniture reference's behaviour graph, within the call, an event: for a sit the first name the caller gives, for a get-up the second (quest_run --furniture-graph-events SIT GET_UP; no event name is stored in the repository). The graph is read when first needed and taken as anim_graph_model_transition_v1 takes PlayAnimation's event, its keys raised under anim_graph_sequence_keys_v1. Sits and get-ups the caller assumes (--assume-sit, --assume-get-up) send nothing. Applied only with --furniture-graph-events (with --anim-graphs and a scripted activation reading); without it no furniture graph event is sent.
origin: Prior general knowledge that a furniture's animation follows its user's. Data (a local probe over the winning FURN records with fo4_scene::anim_graph, outputs outside the repository): 782 winning FURN, 309 distinct models, 93 of them chain to a behaviour graph (224 records); over their root machines' transitions two pairs of names recur as the on and off events of use: the pair given in the forced opening is held by 20 graphs, 9 take its first name from the start state and 22 take its second from at least one state (26 transitions), and another pair is taken from the start state by 12 graphs with 12 off transitions. The player's postwar pod's graph takes the second name of the first pair from its occupied states to the exit sequence whose end key the exit scene's fragment registered for. Weakness: which name the engine sends, and whether it sends one at all, is not in the data; two naming families exist, so the caller chooses; the second of the event against the activation is not settled.
live_measurement: Watch the player leave the postwar pod: the pod's exit animation should begin as the third phase of the exit scene starts and the scene's registration should hear its end key about 16.5 s later (the graph's two sequences); a pod that stays closed or opens at another second refutes the timing.
reason: Behaviour of the running game not measured; the exit step relies on it in the forced opening.

assertion: A placed reference other than an actor that a run moved (a timeline move event, fo4_scene::timeline, recorded from the run's MoveTo reading world_moveto_target_v1) is drawn at the moved position with the rotation and scale its placement stores; one moved to another space, or to a place the run leaves open, is not drawn in the loaded space. Applied only when a frame is drawn from a run timeline (render --timeline, fo4-view --headless --timeline, at --under-hypotheses); without a timeline nothing moves.
origin: The run's world model records only the position a MoveTo with zero offsets gives (world_moveto_target_v1); the native's further argument, which every call of the forced opening passes as true, is not read, so the rotation is kept as stored by choice, not by evidence. In the forced opening every MoveTo receiver is an actor (drawn as a marker), so no reference is drawn moved there.
live_measurement: In a test cell, MoveTo a rotated static or activator onto a marker of another rotation from a script, with the further argument true and then false: the reference keeping its own rotation in both supports it; taking the marker's rotation refutes it for that argument.
reason: Behaviour of the running game not measured; weak: chosen so the frame needs no rotation the run did not record.

assertion: With its switch on (render and fo4-view --timeline-nowait; fo4_scene::timeline::Readings::nowait; off by default), a run's ObjectReference.EnableNoWait and DisableNoWait change a placed reference's presence in a timeline frame as Enable and Disable do under vm_disable_hides_reference_v1 (and its enable children's under xesp_script_change_propagates_v1). Off, a frame counts them and changes nothing for them.
origin: Prior general knowledge of the native names only: a NoWait form differs from the plain native in when the script goes on, not in the end state. The interpreter's data host already answers IsDisabled after DisableNoWait as after Disable; the forced opening calls the NoWait forms 15 times (8 disables, 7 enables), against 45 plain calls.
live_measurement: In a test cell, call DisableNoWait and EnableNoWait on a placed static from a script and photograph it a second later each time: gone, then back, supports it; a reference unchanged refutes it.
reason: Behaviour of the running game not measured; weak-to-medium (names only).

assertion: Actor.GetSitState on the player's handle or a placed actor answers from the run's sitters (fo4_vm::sit): 3 (the documented sitting value) while the run has that actor sitting in a furniture reference, 0 otherwise. Other receivers are left to the host. Applied only with quest_run --sit-state (with --sit-events); without it the native is recorded, undetermined, as before.
origin: Prior general knowledge of the native's documented values (0 not sitting, 3 sitting; the transitional values 2 and 4 are not modelled). Data: the next main quest's door console alias script and the default alias activation script compare the answer with 0 before acting on the player's activation; in the forced run the player got up from the postwar pod before the console activation, so the run's sitters give 0. Weak: the sitting states between a sit and its animation's end are not modelled, and the forced runs only read the answer against 0.
live_measurement: From a test script, log GetSitState on the player before, during and after sitting in a chair: 0, a nonzero value, 0 again support it; a nonzero value while standing refutes it.
reason: Behaviour of the running game not measured; the vault step relies on it in the forced run.

assertion: A placed reference's behaviour graph that the run reads when first needed (anim_graph_model_transition_v1) has played its start state's sequence to its end since the reference loaded: while the current state's sequence has cycle type 2 (read as played once), the first of its text keys in time order that names an event the state itself takes moves the graph along that transition, repeated up to 16 times; it stops at a sequence of another cycle type, a missing sequence, a conditional transition or a key the state does not take. No key is raised to scripts and none is scheduled (when the reference loaded is not known). Applied only with quest_run --anim-graph-start-settled (with --anim-graphs); without it the graph waits in its start state, as before.
origin: Data (a local probe over the winning ACTI, FURN, DOOR and MSTT models that chain to a behaviour graph, outputs outside the repository): 586 graphs read; 41 have a start state playing a sequence of cycle type 2 one of whose own keys names an event that state takes, and 39 of those have no other transition out of the start state, so without this reading no script event could ever move them. The next main quest's door console is one: its start state takes only its own sequence's end key, and the quest's scripts first send it the event its looping successor takes. That cycle type 2 means played once (clamp) is prior knowledge of the NIF format. Weak to medium: the reading assumes the reference loaded long enough before the first script event.
live_measurement: Load a cell with a console of this generic stage graph, then from a test script play its second stage's event a few seconds after load: the panel's second stage animation supports it; nothing happening refutes it (or shows a load-time delay).
reason: Behaviour of the running game not measured; the vault step relies on it in the forced run.

assertion: The sequence a behaviour graph state names (its Gamebryo sequence generator's sequence name) is the model's sequence of that name, or, where none has exactly that name, the first whose name differs from it only in ASCII case (anim_graph_sequence_keys_v1 then schedules its keys). Applied only with quest_run --anim-sequence-case (with --anim-graphs); without it only exact names are found, as before.
origin: Data (the same local probe): of 3,120 states naming a sequence across 586 graphs, 2,206 find it exactly, 162 only ignoring case (in 72 graphs: 34 ACTI, 11 FURN, 27 MSTT models) and 752 not at all. The door console's generic stage graph names its sequences in lower case and the model stores them capitalised. Prior general knowledge that the engine's names are case-insensitive. Medium.
live_measurement: Play the door console's second stage in the running game: the panel moving (its sequence found) supports it; a panel that does not move refutes it.
reason: Behaviour of the running game not measured; the vault step relies on it in the forced run.

assertion: The compiled scripts' equality opcode (15) on two texts that differ only in ASCII case gives true; texts that differ otherwise give false, as before. Applied only with quest_run --text-equal-ignore-case (every mode); without it such a comparison is undetermined under pex_ops_compare_v1, as before.
origin: Prior general knowledge that the scripting language compares strings case-insensitively (its documentation states it). Data: the next main quest's script registers for the door console's key in lower case and its handler compares the event name with the capitalised spelling; the animation case reading (anim_event_name_case_v1) hands the handler the registration's spelling. Medium.
live_measurement: From a test script, log the result of "abc" == "ABC": true supports it; false refutes it.
reason: Behaviour of the running game not measured; the vault step relies on it in the forced run.

assertion: A placed record below the root of its enable parent chain that carries its own flag 0x800, in a chain whose start state under xesp_initial_state_chain_v1, xesp_child_follows_parent_v1 and xesp_flag_bit0_opposite_v1 also starts that record disabled (the flag agrees with the chain), is decided by its chain: it starts disabled, and a run's Enable or Disable of a record above it reaches it through the chain as for any other link (xesp_script_change_propagates_v1). A record whose own flag disagrees with its chain stays undecided. Applied only in a timeline frame with its switch (render and fo4-view --timeline-child-flag-agrees; fo4_scene::timeline::Readings::child_flag_agrees; off by default) to the actors' presence.
origin: A reading of the data, not a measurement: in the forced opening's timeline every actor whose presence a frame leaves undecided (44 of 93 actors the run places) is in one class: the actor carries flag 0x800 itself, its one link carries flag bit 0 (opposite of the parent), and its root is a placed static without flag 0x800, so the flag and the chain both start it disabled; the run then enables or disables that root (spec/timeline-cast-census.txt). Over the load order 866 children carry the flag below an enable parent, 366 of them with a chain that says enabled (spec/enable-parent.md), so about 500 agree. That the flag adds nothing once it agrees is a reading; that the child then follows its parent's later changes is the same claim xesp_child_own_flag_ignored_v1 makes for every such child, narrowed here to the agreeing ones.
live_measurement: In a new game, find a placed actor with its own flag 0x800 under an enable parent with the opposite bit, whose parent a script or the console disables and enables: the actor appearing while the parent is disabled and gone while it is enabled supports it; the actor never appearing refutes it.
reason: Behaviour of the running game not measured; weak-to-medium: the agreement is read from the data, the following of later changes is not.

assertion: An actor a run timeline places somewhere other than its stored position (a package destination, a MoveTo target or a caller's assumed place) is drawn as its character at that position with the rotation its placement (ACHR DATA) stores. Applied only when a frame draws the cast (render and fo4-view --timeline-cast, at --under-hypotheses); an actor at its stored place keeps its placement as before.
origin: The run records only positions (spec/timeline.md): a package destination's location reference, a MoveTo target's position, the caller's point. Which way the actor then faces is not in the timeline; the stored rotation is kept by choice, not by evidence, so the frame needs no rotation the run did not record. In the forced opening 61 of 139 actor places are moves (42 package destinations, 19 MoveTo targets).
live_measurement: Watch an actor walk to a package destination or be moved by MoveTo in a test cell, and photograph which way it faces after: facing as its placement did supports it; facing as the destination marker or the walk's last direction refutes it.
reason: Behaviour of the running game not measured; weak: chosen for want of a recorded rotation.

assertion: With its switch on (render and fo4-view --timeline-target-rotation, with --timeline-cast; fo4_scene::timeline::cast::Options::target_rotation; off by default), an actor a run timeline places somewhere other than its stored position faces as the one placed reference of the loaded cells whose stored position is exactly that place (the move's target: a package's location reference or a MoveTo target) is rotated; with none or several such references the stored rotation is kept under timeline_actor_stored_rotation_v1.
origin: The run's package destinations and MoveTo places are a placed reference's stored position (pack_location_destination_v1, world_moveto_target_v1), so the reference standing exactly there is read back from the position; prior general knowledge that heading markers are placed to give whoever arrives at them a facing. In the forced opening's contact sheet the reading finds exactly one reference at the place for 6 moved actors (10 actor and place pairs; heading markers by their base) and none in the loaded cells for 14 others. Nothing in the data says which rotation the actor takes.
live_measurement: In a test cell, MoveTo an actor onto a heading marker rotated away from the actor, and let a package send another actor to a rotated marker; photograph both: facing as the markers supports it; keeping their own rotation refutes it.
reason: Behaviour of the running game not measured; weak: prior knowledge only.

assertion: With its switch on (render and fo4-view --actor-missing-bone-bind, with --timeline-cast; fo4_scene::actor::Actor::missing_bones_at_bind, fo4_scene::timeline::cast::Options::missing_bones_at_bind; off by default), a bone a skinned shape of an actor's model names that the actor's skeleton does not hold is skinned at its bind transform: its matrix is the identity, so the vertices it carries keep the positions the model stores, blended with the other bones as actor_skin_linear_blend_v1 blends them; off, such a shape fails the actor (ActorSkinBoneMissing).
origin: A reading of the data: the bones a skinned shape names come with their inverse bind transform (BSSkin::BoneData), so the bind pose is known for every bone even where the race's skeleton lacks it; in the forced opening's contact sheet 25 of 38 actors the cast could not draw failed only on such bones (cloth and hair bones, by their names), and 3 heads on a hair bone. Prior general knowledge that such bones are moved at run time by a cloth or physics system the data here does not drive; at rest that motion is absent, so the bind place is the reading that adds nothing.
live_measurement: Photograph an actor wearing such an outfit standing still in a test cell from four sides: cloth and hair hanging where the model stores them (as bound) supports it; cloth and hair settled elsewhere (gravity, wind) refutes it for a frame at rest.
reason: Behaviour of the running game not measured; weak: it draws the parts as bound rather than as the game moves them.

assertion: An interior cell's surfaces are lit by the cell's stored Ambient Color (added everywhere) and its Directional Color along one direction: the unit vector toward the light is (cos XY cos Z, cos XY sin Z, sin XY) with XY and Z the stored Directional Rotation XY and Z in degrees (Z counter-clockwise about +Z from +X, XY raising it above the horizontal plane), weighted by the cosine with the surface's normal, never below zero. Directional Fade, the directional ambient colours and the light fade distances of CELL.XCLL are not read. Applied only with its switch (render and fo4-view --light-cell; fo4_scene::light::Switches::cell; off by default) to interior cells.
origin: The fields and their layout are sourced (spec/record-layouts.tsv, CELL.XCLL); that they light surfaces this way is a reading: the colours are taken as linear values over 255, ambient added, directional by the cosine law. The rotation's axes are not in the data: chosen as the simplest reading of two angles named XY and Z. In the light census the run's one interior cell stores ambient 52,61,65 and directional 11,17,21 at rotation 0 and 270 (spec/light-census.txt), so the directional term is small there.
live_measurement: In an interior test cell with no placed light, author an ambient colour and a strong directional colour at rotation XY 0 and Z 0, then Z 90; photograph a cube with known albedo from fixed angles: faces brightening in the order the formula gives supports it; another order, or no change with the directional colour, refutes it.
reason: Behaviour of the running game not measured; weak: the combination and the axes are the simplest reading, not read.

assertion: An interior cell that names a lighting template (LTMP, an LGTM) takes from the template's DATA the fields its own XCLL Inherits word names by printed label (Ambient Color, Directional Color, Fog Color for both fog colours, Fog Near, Fog Far, Directional Rotation, Fog Max; the other labels name fields the light step does not read); a word whose labels are not fully named takes nothing; a cell with a template and no XCLL takes every field from the template. Applied only with its switch (render and fo4-view --light-inherits, with --light-cell or --light-fog; off by default).
origin: The word-to-label correspondences are transcribed from the naming source's printed values (spec/record-flag-words.tsv); that a named field comes from the template is the reading of the word Inherits, not a measurement. In the run's interior cell the word names Fog Near, Fog Far, Directional Rotation, Directional Fade, Clip Distance, Fog Max and Light Fade Distances, so the fog distances come from the template (500 to 4600 instead of 300 to 3500; spec/light-census.txt).
live_measurement: Author two interior cells with the same template and different own fog distances, one whose Inherits word names Fog Near and Fog Far and one whose word does not; photograph the same corridor in both: the first matching the template's fog and the second its own supports it; the reverse, or both alike, refutes it.
reason: Behaviour of the running game not measured; weak-to-medium: the labels are printed by the naming source, the meaning is the word's.

assertion: A placed light (a reference whose base is a LIGH with DATA, not left out by the enable parent rules) lights a surface point at distance d below its radius R with its stored colour times (1 - d / R) times the cosine between the surface's normal and the direction to the light, never below zero; at and beyond R it adds nothing. Every light is a point: the type labels (spot, hemisphere, omnidirectional), FOV, near clip, flicker, the falloff exponent field and shadows are not read. Applied only with its switch (render and fo4-view --light-points; off by default).
origin: The radius and colour are stored (LIGH.DATA, spec/record-layouts.tsv); the curve is not in the data: linear with a cut at the radius is the first family of spec/light-measurement.md, chosen as the simplest that ends at the stored radius; the light measurement's decision not to read the field named Falloff Exponent is kept. In the light census the run's interior cell places 382 lights (8 spot labels, 1 omnidirectional label, the rest without a type label), radius 128 to 1024 (spec/light-census.txt).
live_measurement: The bench of spec/light-measurement.md: one light at heights 0.125 R to 1.5 R above a flat neutral floor, linear calibrated captures: a centre brightness proportional to 1 - q with zero at q >= 1 supports it; the power or inverse-square families of that table refute it.
reason: Behaviour of the running game not measured; weak: the curve is a choice, spots are drawn as points.

assertion: A placed light whose reference stores XRDS has the radius its base stores plus the XRDS value (an adjustment, not a replacement). Applied only with its switch (render and fo4-view --light-reference-radius, with --light-points; off by default).
origin: A reading of the data: XRDS is a sourced f32 (spec/record-layouts.tsv, REFR.XRDS); in the light census 457 of the run's 465 placed lights store it, and its value over the base radius lies between -0.91 and 4.4 with median -0.30 and -0.37 in the interior and exterior cells (spec/light-census.txt): negative in most, never at or below -1, which fits an amount added to a radius that stays positive and does not fit a radius of its own.
live_measurement: Place one light base twice in a test cell, once without XRDS and once with a negative XRDS of half its radius; photograph the floor under both: the second's lit circle half as wide supports it; a lit circle as wide as the first, or none, refutes it.
reason: Behaviour of the running game not measured; medium-weak: the sign pattern is read, the use is not.

assertion: A placed light's colour is multiplied by its base's fade value (LIGH FNAM, an f32) before it lights anything. Applied only with its switch (render and fo4-view --light-fade, with --light-points; off by default).
origin: The field is sourced (LIGH.FNAM, spec/record-layouts.tsv); its use as an intensity is prior general knowledge from the label alone. In the light census its value is 0.2 to 1.3 in the interior cell (median 1.2) and 0.5 to 1 outside (spec/light-census.txt).
live_measurement: Place two copies of one light base differing only in fade value (0.5 and 1) above a neutral floor; calibrated captures: the centre's light term halving supports it; equal brightness refutes it.
reason: Behaviour of the running game not measured; weak: prior knowledge of the label only.

assertion: An interior cell's lit surfaces are mixed toward its Fog Color Near by the fraction min(clamp((d - Fog Near) / (Fog Far - Fog Near), 0, 1), Fog Max) at distance d from the eye; Fog Color Far, Fog Power, the height fog fields and Fog Clip Distance are not read; the sky and unlit surfaces are not fogged. Applied only with its switch (render and fo4-view --light-fog; off by default) to interior cells.
origin: The fields are sourced (CELL.XCLL); the curve is the simplest reading of a near and far distance and a maximum, not read. The run's interior cell stores fog 300 to 3500 (500 to 4600 from its template under cell_light_template_inherits_v1) with maximum 0.7 and power 1.2 (spec/light-census.txt).
live_measurement: Photograph a long interior corridor of a cell with known fog values at several distances, calibrated: a mix proportional to the distance between near and far, capped at the maximum, supports it; a curved mix (the power field) or none refutes it.
reason: Behaviour of the running game not measured; weak.

assertion: A lit surface's colour is its unlit colour (texture, vertex colour, effect tint) times the sum of the light terms in linear values, then mixed with the fog, then held within 0 to 1 as before; no tone mapping, exposure, image space or bloom. Surfaces of effect shaders, the run's placeholder markers and the sky are drawn unlit. The surface's normal is the triangle's face normal turned toward the eye (presentation: vertex normals and normal maps are not read). Applied whenever a light switch lights a frame (render and fo4-view).
origin: Nothing in the data says how the game maps light to the frame: the cell's image space record (IMGS) stores fields not read here (spec/light-census.txt). Multiplying and clamping is the simplest reading and keeps an unlit surface (light 1) as before.
live_measurement: Photograph a neutral surface under one light at increasing light colours: a frame value proportional to the light until it clips supports it; a curved response (a tone curve or exposure) refutes it.
reason: Behaviour of the running game not measured; weak: the game certainly tone maps; this is the simplest reading.

assertion: An exterior cell's worldspace climate (WRLD CNAM) that lists one weather (one WLST entry) has that weather. A climate listing several has none unless the caller names one (--assume-weather N, the entry's index). A region's weather data is not read. Applied whenever an exterior weather switch is on (render and fo4-view --sky-weather, --light-weather, --fog-weather).
origin: A reading of the data: every CLMT WLST of the load order is a whole number of 12-byte entries whose first word resolves to a WTHR (fo4_plugin::weather); 9 of 11 climates list one weather, among them the run's exterior climate (second word 100, third word zero); the regions the run's exterior cells name hold no weather subrecord (spec/light-census.txt).

reason: Behaviour of the running game not measured; medium: one weather is listed, how the game picks one is not read.

assertion: The caller's hour (--assume-hour H) reads one slot of the weather's tables: the climate's TNAM first four bytes are times of day in tens of minutes (t0 to t3); before t0 and from t3 on, slot 3; from t0, slot 0; from t1, slot 1; from t2, slot 2. No blending between slots; slots 4 to 7 are never read. Applied whenever an exterior weather switch is on with the caller's hour.
origin: The bytes and the count of slots are in the data: TNAM is six bytes whose first four rise (30, 54, 102, 126: 5:00, 9:00, 17:00, 21:00 in tens of minutes); the weather stores 8 DALC, 8 IMSP and 19 colour rows of 8 (spec/light-census.txt). Slot 3 is the darkest in every row and slot 1 the brightest directional ambient, which fits night and day; the order sunrise, day, sunset, night of the first four slots and the unit of the times are prior general knowledge.
live_measurement: Set the hour to 7, 12, 19 and 23 in the run's exterior and photograph the sky straight up and the horizon: colours matching slots 0, 1, 2 and 3 of the weather's rows supports it; another order or blended colours refutes it in part.
reason: Behaviour of the running game not measured; weak: the slot order is prior knowledge with a data hint.

assertion: An exterior frame's background (where no surface is drawn) is a gradient by the sine s of the view direction's elevation: the weather's colour row 8 at the horizon and below (s <= 0), row 7 at s = 0.25, row 0 at the zenith (s = 1), linear between (the stops' elevations are presentation), at the slot climate_hour_slot_v1 gives. Clouds, sun, moon and stars are not drawn. Applied only with its switch (render and fo4-view --sky-weather, with --assume-hour; off by default) to exterior frames.
origin: The table is in the data (19 rows of 8 four-byte colours, fourth byte zero); which rows are sky is not: rows 0, 7 and 8 are taken as zenith, lower sky and horizon from prior general knowledge of the table's order, with a data hint: at the day slot row 0 is the darkest blue, row 7 a lighter blue and row 8 a warm pale colour, the order a clear sky shows from zenith to horizon; rows 1 and 17 and rows 12 and 18 repeat each other but for one slot, rows 2, 10 and 11 are zero (spec/light-census.txt).
live_measurement: Photograph the clear sky of the run's exterior at noon from the ground looking up, at 45 degrees and at the horizon: colours close to rows 0, 7 and 8 of the day slot (allowing for the tone mapping light_sum_clamped_v1 leaves out) support it; colours of other rows refute it.
reason: Behaviour of the running game not measured; weak: the row roles are prior knowledge.

assertion: An exterior frame's lit surfaces receive the weather's directional ambient (DALC, read with the sourced LGTM.DALC layout) of the slot climate_hour_slot_v1 gives, times its Scale, as an ambient cube: a normal's component toward +X reads the X- entry and toward -X the X+ entry (likewise Y and Z), weighted by the component's square. No sun or moon light: the data stores no direction for it. Applied only with its switch (render and fo4-view --light-weather, with --assume-hour; off by default) to exterior frames.

The square weights are the simplest blend of six colours.
live_measurement: Photograph a white cube in open ground at noon on a clear day, four sides and top: the top lit near the day slot's Z- colour and the sides near their opposite entries supports it; the top near Z+ refutes the facing reading.
reason: Behaviour of the running game not measured; weak-to-medium: the facing is read from the colours, the blend is chosen.

assertion: An exterior frame's lit surfaces are mixed toward the weather's colour row 1 at the slot climate_hour_slot_v1 gives by the fraction min(clamp((d - near) / (far - near), 0, 1), max) at distance d from the eye, with near, far and max the weather's FNAM values 1, 2 and 7 (in stored order, from 1) for slots 0 to 2 and 3, 4 and 8 for slot 3. assertion: A standing actor that nothing has acted on plays the clip its race's behaviour graph reaches from its root by: each state machine's start state (where the start state is bound to a variable, that variable's stored initial value), the generator a modifier, tagging or offset generator holds (an offset generator's own offset clip is not drawn), a blender's child of the highest weight (a weight bound to a variable takes the variable's stored initial value; the first of equal weights), a manual selector's stored index (or its variable's), a behaviour reference's file under the project's folder, down to a clip generator, drawn at that generator's stored start time. Every reaching path passes one blender whose two children share weight 1 (the second a bone-weighted camera layer), taken in order.

origin: The earlier tracks were the caller's (navmesh heights, straight moves between waypoints); the walker is this project's own controller (spec/walk.md) and no source says which point of the player the game's triggers and distance natives test.
live_measurement: Walk the player across the edge of a trigger box whose bottom face lies a few units above the floor, logging player.getpos and the second OnTriggerEnter fires, in two launches: getpos z at the floor under the capsule and the event at the crossing of that point (with the body reading) support it; an event when the eye or the capsule's side meets the box refutes it.

assertion: In the play mode the quest run's real-time clock (scene clock, timers, line seconds, the track's seconds) is the play clock: one second of the scripted input, or one second of a window frame's wall time, is one second of the run, from second 0 of the new game; the run advances only to the second its input has reached.
covered_causes: fo4-play stepped clock loop (run seconds = input seconds)
origin: The run's clock was the caller's track's seconds; nothing measured relates the game's script clock to frame time (pauses, menus, loading, frame-rate limits are not modelled).
live_measurement: Start a new game with a stopwatch on screen capture; walk into the first trigger the opening's walk crosses; the second its stage is set (quest log or console getstage polling) against the capture's second, in two launches: equal within a frame supports it; a lag that grows with loading or menus refutes it as stated.

assertion: In the play mode the activation input activates the placed reference whose collision primitive (as fo4-walk builds it) the ray from the walker's eye along the view direction meets first within the caller's reach; terrain or a primitive of no reference stops the ray and activates nothing; the primitives of references the run disabled are passed through.
origin: The ray from the eye is how a crosshair is commonly understood (prior knowledge, not data); the reach is the caller's number (no data of this step gives it); references without placed collision cannot be met (see play_activate_object_bounds_v1).
live_measurement: Aim at a door past the edge of a table and of a wall at several distances, noting which reference the activation prompt names and the largest distance it appears at, in two launches: the first object along the eye's line supports it; a prompt for an object behind a nearer collision, or at a reach that differs per object type, refutes or bounds it.

assertion: With its switch on (play_run --play-pick-bounds; off by default), the activation ray also meets the box of the object bounds (OBND, six i16: low and high corner in model units) of each placed reference of the walked cells that the walking world holds no collision for, placed by the reference's position, rotation and scale; the nearer of the collision hit and the box hit wins, a tie going to the collision.
covered_causes: fo4-play pick (references without placed collision, doors among them)
origin: The opening's front door has no placed collision under this project's collision rules (CollisionNotReady), so the collision ray cannot reach it; OBND is read as a format fact (spec/plugin.md) but its use as the activation volume is a guess.
live_measurement: Aim just inside and just outside a door's OBND box corners (computed from its record) at close range and note whether the activation prompt appears: a prompt inside the box and none outside supports it; a prompt outside the box, or none inside it, refutes it.
